sentences.zh: 它允许政客们跨越这个新统一国家的各个阶层进行诉求，吸引城市里的工人、农民、城市知识分子以及诸如此类的人群。

sentences.en: And it's from that expression that we get irredentism.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，德国也有类似的情况。

sentences.en: So this idea that there's unfinished national business, that we need to complete the nation.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is an idea that's politically very effective in the late 19th century.
sentences.zh: 现在，和德国人一样，意大利人觉得自己完成统一的时间稍微有点太晚了。

sentences.en: It allows politicians to appeal across this newly united country to different classes, to workers in their cities, to farmers, to urban intellectuals, all of this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 我们想要里雅斯特和戈里齐亚这两座城市。

sentences.en: And as you said, there is a parallel in Germany.
sentences.zh: 理想情况下，我想，我们希望拥有斯洛文尼亚。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为许多现代克罗地亚也确实应该成为意大利的一部分。

sentences.en: Now, rather like the Germans, the Italians feel they've united a little bit too late.
sentences.zh: 所以他们想要——

sentences.en: They've been shut out of the scramble for foreign colonies, for example, in Africa.
sentences.zh: 比方说在非洲，他们在争夺外国殖民地的竞争中被排挤在外。

sentences.en: And if they want to be a great power, they need colonists.
sentences.zh: 如果他们想成为一个大国，就需要殖民地。

sentences.en: So they look to North Africa initially.
sentences.zh: 所以他们最初把目光投向了北非。

sentences.en: Tom, obviously, this is Tom Horan Bingo.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，显然，这就是汤姆·霍兰宾果游戏。

sentences.en: The example of the Roman Empire is hanging over them the whole time.
sentences.zh: 罗马帝国的例子始终萦绕在他们心头。

sentences.en: They want to basically rebuild the Roman Empire as much as possible.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上想尽可能地重修罗马帝国。

sentences.en: They look to North Africa.
sentences.zh: 他们将目光投向北非。

sentences.en: But to their horror, a much bigger power has already got stuck in in North Africa, and that's France.
sentences.zh: 但令他们惊恐的是，一个更强大的力量已经率先介入了北非，那就是法国。

sentences.en: And actually, the French make it pretty obvious they don't want the Italians getting involved.
sentences.zh: 事实上，法国人表现得非常明显，他们不希望意大利人插手。

sentences.en: And there's a bit of rivalry between the French and the Italians in North Africa.
sentences.zh: 法国和意大利在北非之间存在着一些竞争。

sentences.en: And as a result of that, the Italians sign a very implausible alliance in 1882.
sentences.zh: 正因为如此，意大利人在1882年签署了一个极其荒谬的同盟。

sentences.en: First of all, with Germany, that's not so implausible.
sentences.zh: 首先是与德国，这个倒还算不上那么荒谬。

sentences.en: But Austria, but with Austria as well.
sentences.zh: 还有奥地利，竟然也和奥地利结盟。

sentences.en: That's mad.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And this is basically to give them a bit more of a free hand in Africa, so that the French won't attack them.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是为了给他们在非洲提供更多一点的行动自由，好让法国人不会攻击他们。

sentences.en: And it's called the Triple Alliance.
sentences.zh: 这个同盟被称为三国同盟。

sentences.en: A lot of nationalists are very uneasy about it.
sentences.zh: 许多民族主义者对此感到非常不安。

sentences.en: What are we getting into bed with the Austrians for?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么要跟奥地利人混在一起？

sentences.en: They're our enemies.
sentences.zh: 他们是我们的敌人。

sentences.en: However, the upside, this allows Italy to pursue some colonial adventures.
sentences.zh: 然而，好的一面是，这允许意大利去追求一些殖民冒险。

sentences.en: So in Eritrea, in Somaliland, in Abyssinia, Ethiopia, and most obviously in Libya.
sentences.zh: 所以在厄立特里亚、索马里兰、阿比西尼亚、埃塞俄比亚，最明显的是在利比亚。

sentences.en: And these go generally very badly.
sentences.zh: 而这些行动总体上都非常糟糕。

sentences.en: I mean, the Italians do make inroads, but their army consistently performs very badly.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，意大利人确实取得了一些进展，但他们的军队表现一直非常糟糕。

sentences.en: So in Abyssinia, 6,000 Italian soldiers were massacred in a single day at the Battle of Adwa in 1896.
sentences.zh: 所以在阿比西尼亚，1896年的阿杜瓦战役中，有6000名意大利士兵在一天之内遭到屠杀。

sentences.en: And there's still a sense when you get into the 20th century that nationalist ambitions have not been sated, that Italy still needs to prove its virility on the world stage.
sentences.zh: 进入20世纪后，人们仍然有一种感觉，即民族主义的野心尚未得到满足，意大利仍然需要在世界舞台上证明其雄风。

sentences.en: Yeah, because in Rome at this point, they're building an enormous monument on the Capitol, which is the great sacred hill of Rome.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为此时在罗马，他们正在卡比托利欧山上建造一座巨大的纪念碑，那是罗马伟大的神圣山丘。

sentences.en: And this is a monument to Victor Emmanuel II, who'd been the king when Italy had been united.
sentences.zh: 这是为了纪念维托里奥·埃马努埃莱二世，他曾是意大利统一时的国王。

sentences.en: And there's a sense, I mean, anyone who's been to
sentences.zh: 这种感觉，我的意思是，任何去过

sentences.en: Rome will immediately be able to picture it.
sentences.zh: 罗马的人都能立刻在脑海中浮现出它的画面。

sentences.en: It looks like something out of a Cecil B.
sentences.zh: 它看起来就像是小塞西尔·B·

sentences.en: de Mill film about ancient Rome.
sentences.zh: 德米尔关于古罗马的电影里的布景。

sentences.en: It's kind of symbolically illustrating the fusion between the unity of
sentences.zh: 它在某种程度上象征性地说明了意大利的统一

sentences.en: Italy and this kind of glorious Roman past, which it is assumed a united Italy will be able to resurrect.
sentences.zh: 与这种光荣的罗马过去的融合，而人们认为统一后的意大利将能够重现这种过去。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And that's not completed, I think, until 1911.
sentences.zh: 我想，这个工程直到1911年才完工。

sentences.en: So just before the outbreak of the war.
sentences.zh: 也就是战争爆发前夕。

sentences.en: It's a monstrosity, actually, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 事实上，这是一个怪物，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a wedding cake.
sentences.zh: 它就是一个婚礼蛋糕。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think, yes, I think absolutely right that the sense of becoming a great power and building a united nation, that those two things are interfused.
sentences.zh: 我想，是的，我完全赞同这种说法：成为一个大国和建立一个统一国家的意识，这两者是交织在一起的。

sentences.en: And there's this sort of sense of unfinished business, this sense of pressure and of slight disappointment almost hanging over the Italian project as you enter the
sentences.zh: 当你跨入

sentences.en: 20th century.
sentences.zh: 20世纪时，意大利的事业中弥漫着一种未竟的事业感、一种压力感以及几乎带有一点失望的情绪。

sentences.en: Now, at this point, Italy is changing a lot.
sentences.zh: 此时，意大利正在发生巨大的变化。

sentences.en: It's industrializing, it's building railways and schools.
sentences.zh: 它正在实现工业化，修建铁路和学校。

sentences.en: It is, however, a long way behind the other so-called great powers.
sentences.zh: 然而，它远远落后于其他所谓的列强。

sentences.en: It's only got a very small urban middle class.
sentences.zh: 它只有极少数的城市中产阶级。

sentences.en: The vast majority of Italians work on the land as peasants.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数意大利人作为农民在土地上劳作。

sentences.en: Literacy rates are very low.
sentences.zh: 识字率非常低。

sentences.en: Infant mortality is very high.
sentences.zh: 婴儿死亡率非常高。

sentences.en: The state, most people only have a very vague sense of what the state is.
sentences.zh: 对于国家，大多数人只有一种非常模糊的概念，不知道国家是什么。

sentences.en: Their horizons are bounded by the locality, by the village, by the farm, all of this.
sentences.zh: 他们的视野局限于当地、村庄、农场，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And only a tiny fraction of the population gets to vote.
sentences.zh: 只有极小一部分人口拥有投票权。

sentences.en: So in 1913, 8 million people out of 35 million people.
sentences.zh: 所以在1913年，在3500万人口中只有800万人有投票权。

sentences.en: Politics is a sort of endless, as always in Italy, an endless sort of dance of coalition building.
sentences.zh: 正如意大利一贯的那样，政治是一种无休止的、类似组阁联盟的无休止舞蹈。

sentences.en: Politicians who are constantly kind of ditching their principles to meet the demands of the moment.
sentences.zh: 政客们为了迎合当下的需求，不断地抛弃自己的原则。

sentences.en: And at the top is the king, Victor Emmanuel III.
sentences.zh: 而最高统治者是国王维托里奥·埃马努埃莱三世。

sentences.en: So he's the grandson of the monument guy.
sentences.zh: 所以他是那个纪念碑主角的孙子。

sentences.en: He is.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he is a very short man.
sentences.zh: 他个子非常矮。

sentences.en: He's very short.
sentences.zh: 他真的很矮。

sentences.en: He's very insecure.
sentences.zh: 他非常缺乏安全感。

sentences.en: He's a coin collector.
sentences.zh: 他是个硬币收藏家。

sentences.en: So he's like you, Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以他就像你一样，汤姆。

sentences.en: Collects coins.
sentences.zh: 收集硬币。

sentences.en: He fancies himself as an amateur photographer.
sentences.zh: 他自诩为业余摄影师。

sentences.en: That's his passion.
sentences.zh: 那是他的激情所在。

sentences.en: He has loads of power under the Italian constitution.
sentences.zh: 根据意大利宪法，他拥有巨大的权力。

sentences.en: So he can call parliament, dismiss parliament.
sentences.zh: 所以他可以召集议会、解散议会。

sentences.en: He can appoint the ministers.
sentences.zh: 他可以任命大臣。

sentences.en: He directs foreign policy.
sentences.zh: 他指导外交政策。

sentences.en: He commands the army.
sentences.zh: 他指挥军队。

sentences.en: He declares war.
sentences.zh: 他宣战。

sentences.en: But he doesn't like using his power.
sentences.zh: 但他不喜欢使用自己的权力。

sentences.en: In fact, he wants politicians to do it for him.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他希望政客们代劳。

sentences.en: And this in the long run will get him into trouble because he'll basically turn himself into Benito Mussolini's puppet in the 1920s and 1930s.
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，这会给他带来麻烦，因为在20世纪20年代和30年代，他基本上把自己变成了贝尼托·墨索里尼的傀儡。

sentences.en: But at this point, let's go to 1914 when the First World War begins.
sentences.zh: 但此时，让我们回到1914年第一次世界大战爆发的时候。

sentences.en: At this point, his prime minister is a man called Antonio Salandra.
sentences.zh: 当时，他的首相是一个名叫安东尼奥·萨兰德拉的人。

sentences.en: And Salandra is a conservative lawyer from a rich family, land-owning family in Puglia in the south of Italy.
sentences.zh: 萨兰德拉是一位保守派律师，出身于意大利南部普利亚的富裕地主家庭。

sentences.en: But he's backed by the big business elites in the industrial north because he's a conservative.
sentences.zh: 但他得到了工业北方大企业精英的支持，因为他是一名保守派。

sentences.en: He's a sort of balding man with this absolutely gigantic moustache, exactly as you would want.
sentences.zh: 他是个谢顶的男人，留着一撮绝对巨大的胡子，完全符合你的想象。

sentences.en: Oh, thank God.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢天谢地。

sentences.en: It's so good to have an enormous moustache back on the rest of his history.
sentences.zh: 历史的后续里能重新出现一大撮胡子真是太好了。

sentences.en: It is, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然是的。

sentences.en: Haven't had one for a while.
sentences.zh: 好一阵子没看到了。

sentences.en: He's a very ruthless and devious man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常冷酷无情、阴险狡诈的人。

sentences.en: And he is the man who is basically going to act as the head of the conspiracy to drag Italy into the war against the wishes of its people.
sentences.zh: 他基本上将充当阴谋集团的头目，违背人民意愿将意大利拖入战争。

sentences.en: Now, when Franz
sentences.zh: 现在，当弗朗茨

sentences.en: Ferdinand was assassinated in the summer of 1914, Italy was going through all kinds of internal
sentences.zh: 斐迪南在1914年夏天被暗杀时，意大利正经历着各种内部

sentences.en: ructions, massive strikes, unrest, talk of socialist and anarchist revolution and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 动乱、大规模罢工、骚乱，以及关于社会主义和无政府主义革命的言论等等。

sentences.en: So Salandra was distracted.
sentences.zh: 所以萨兰德拉分心了。

sentences.en: But his foreign minister, who was the Marquis of San Giuliano, who was a Sicilian aristocrat, said to the Austrians, I know we're in this alliance with you,
sentences.zh: 但他的外交大臣圣朱利亚诺侯爵（他是一位西西里贵族）对奥地利人说，我知道我们与你们有这个同盟，

sentences.en: but if you attack Serbia, we will not support you.
sentences.zh: 但如果你们进攻塞尔维亚，我们不会支持你们。

sentences.en: And the reason we don't want to support you, well, basically, the Italians don't want to see Austria expand in the Balkans.
sentences.zh: 我们不想支持你们的原因是，基本上，意大利人不愿意看到奥地利在巴尔干地区扩张。

sentences.en: Become more powerful.
sentences.zh: 变得更加强大。

sentences.en: I mean, that would be mad.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那太疯狂了。

sentences.en: No, they don't.
sentences.zh: 不，他们不愿意。

sentences.en: And they say, we might accept you attacking Serbia if you gave us the South
sentences.zh: 他们说，如果你们把南蒂罗尔

sentences.en: Tyrell.
sentences.zh: 割让给我们，我们或许可以接受你们进攻塞尔维亚。

sentences.en: And the Germans actually said to the Austrians, would you think about it?
sentences.zh: 德国人实际上对奥地利人说，你们考虑一下吗？

sentences.en: And the
sentences.zh: 而

sentences.en: Austrians said, hold on, we're about to enter a war to defend our empire.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人说，等等，我们正要为了保卫帝国而参战。

sentences.en: We're not going to start giving bits away to our random neighbors.
sentences.zh: 我们可不会开始把领土分给随便哪个邻居。

sentences.en: So the First World War starts and Italy declares itself neutral.
sentences.zh: 于是第一次世界大战爆发了，意大利宣布保持中立。

sentences.en: Now, under the Triple Alliance, they didn't actually have to join the war, because the Triple Alliance was meant to be a defensive pact, not an offensive one.
sentences.zh: 根据三国同盟，他们实际上不必参战，因为三国同盟本应是一个防御性条约，而非进攻性条约。

sentences.en: But I guess it's kind of against the spirit, if not the letter.
sentences.zh: 但我想这多多少有点违背了精神，如果不是违背了字面意思的话。

sentences.en: It is a bit.
sentences.zh: 确实有点。

sentences.en: I think the Austrians and the Germans are disappointed.
sentences.zh: 我想奥地利人和德国人很失望。

sentences.en: They say, well, this is really poor from the Italians.
sentences.zh: 他们说，意大利人做得实在太差劲了。

sentences.en: On the other hand, it's the Italians.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，他们毕竟是意大利人。

sentences.en: So, you know, you kind of know what you're getting into when you sign an alliance with them.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，跟他们结盟时你就该知道会面临什么。

sentences.en: And the Italians said, well, you took us for granted.
sentences.zh: 而意大利人则说，你们把我们视为理所当然。

sentences.en: You didn't consult us.
sentences.zh: 你们没有征求我们的意见。

sentences.en: You've got stuck in.
sentences.zh: 你们已经陷进去了。

sentences.en: And there's also good reasons for Italy to stay out.
sentences.zh: 而且意大利袖手旁观也有充足的理由。

sentences.en: A public opinion.
sentences.zh: 公众舆论。

sentences.en: People don't like the
sentences.zh: 人们不喜欢

sentences.en: Austrians.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人。

sentences.en: Also, Italy imports a lot of raw materials, including, this is a terrible indictment of Italian agriculture, including food from Britain and France.
sentences.zh: 此外，意大利进口大量原材料，其中包括——这是对意大利农业的沉重控诉——包括来自英国和法国的粮食。

sentences.en: So if they entered the war on the side of the central powers, the British and French would probably blockade their ports
sentences.zh: 因此，如果他们站在同盟国一边参战，英法两国可能会封锁他们的港口

sentences.en: and people would starve and that would be a right mess and they don't fancy that.
sentences.zh: 人们就会挨饿，那将是一团糟，他们可不想这样。

sentences.en: So they say, we're going to sit this one out.
sentences.zh: 所以他们说，这场我们不掺和。

sentences.en: Fine.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Just a week later, the Marquis of San Giuliano sends
sentences.zh: 仅仅一周后，圣朱利亚诺侯爵给

sentences.en: Salandra a note and he says, I've been thinking, I think if the allies look like they're going to win, we should actually switch sides and pile in on their side against Austria.
sentences.zh: 萨兰德拉发了一张便条，上面写道，我一直在考虑，如果协约国看起来要赢，我们实际上应该倒戈，加入他们的阵营共同对付奥地利。

sentences.en: And the Marquis has the excellent line.
sentences.zh: 侯爵有一句绝妙的名言。

sentences.en: This may not be heroic, but it is wise and patriotic.
sentences.zh: 这或许算不上英雄主义，但却是明智且爱国的。

sentences.en: And the same day, so the 9th of August, the Marquis of San Giuliano starts to send our informal messages to London.
sentences.zh: 同一天，也就是8月9日，圣朱利亚诺侯爵开始向伦敦发送非正式信息。

sentences.en: If we were to change sides, would you?
sentences.zh: 如果我们改变立场，你们会……？

sentences.en: Yeah, just, just wondering.
sentences.zh: 对，就是，只是想知道。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, they say to the chief military commander, General Cadorna, who we'll talk about in the second half, your plans for war against France.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，他们对最高军事指挥官卡多纳将军（我们将在下半场讨论他）说，你们针对法国的作战计划。

sentences.en: Just shift them.
sentences.zh: 直接调整一下。

sentences.en: Yeah, just update them a little bit.
sentences.zh: 对，稍微更新一下。

sentences.en: So it's war now against Austria.
sentences.zh: 所以现在的敌人是对奥地利作战。

sentences.en: Anyway, a month passes.
sentences.zh: 总之，一个月过去了。

sentences.en: The Germans, of course, have launched their great attack on France and they've been turned back at the River Marne, the Battle of the Marne.
sentences.zh: 德国人当然对法国发动了重大进攻，并在马恩河（马恩河战役）被击退了。

sentences.en: And Salandra says to his cronies, we should use this historic cataclysm to, and I quote, complete and enlarge the fatherland.
sentences.zh: 萨兰德拉对他的亲信们说，我们应该利用这场历史性的大灾难来，请允许我引用原话，完善和扩大祖国。

sentences.en: And, you know, he acknowledges, people will say that we've been very sneaky and perfidious, but he says, Italy's destiny should be guided by, and he uses the phrase, sacro egoismo,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他承认，人们会说我们非常狡猾和背信弃义，但他表示，意大利的命运应该由——他用了这个词——sacro egoismo来指导，

sentences.en: sacred egoism.
sentences.zh: 即神圣利己主义。

sentences.en: And this becomes one of the most famous phrases in modern Italian history.
sentences.zh: 这成为了现代意大利历史上最著名的短语之一。

sentences.en: And that idea of sacred egoism expresses the, dare I say, the sacral quality of Italian nationalism.
sentences.zh: 神圣利己主义的概念表达了，恕我直言，意大利民族主义的神圣特质。

sentences.en: Sacral, sacral poor behavior.
sentences.zh: 神圣的，神圣的糟糕行为。

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: That they believe they have a kind of divinely appointed mission to complete the unification of the nation.
sentences.zh: 他们相信自己有一种神圣委任的使命来完成国家的统一。

sentences.en: And if that involves taking large parts of other people's countries.
sentences.zh: 如果这涉及到夺取别人国家的大片领土。

sentences.en: And stabbing them in the back.
sentences.zh: 并在背后捅刀子。

sentences.en: So much the better.
sentences.zh: 那就再好不过了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's now a long complicated diplomatic dance.
sentences.zh: 于是现在展开了一场漫长而复杂的外交舞蹈。

sentences.en: In January 1915, Salandra sends a message to Vienna and he says,
sentences.zh: 1915年1月，萨兰德拉向维也纳发去信息，上面写着，

sentences.en: I'd like you to give us Trento, the Trentino, this sort of area in the north and South Tyrol.
sentences.zh: 我希望你们把特伦托、特伦蒂诺（北方这一带）以及南蒂罗尔割让给我们。

sentences.en: We'd like a bit of Slovenia, please.
sentences.zh: 我们想要一点斯洛文尼亚，谢谢。

sentences.en: And we'd like Trieste to be neutral and autonomous.
sentences.zh: 而我们希望的里雅斯特保持中立和自治。

sentences.en: The Austrians really like Trieste because it's their one big port.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人真的很喜欢的里雅斯特，因为这是他们唯一的大港口。

sentences.en: They don't want to give that away.
sentences.zh: 他们不想拱手让人。

sentences.en: And the Austrians say, I'm not going to give you all that.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人则表示，我才不会把所有这些都给你。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: You were an ally only recently.
sentences.zh: 你们不久前还是盟友呢。

sentences.en: We're not going to give you large pits of our empire.
sentences.zh: 我们不会把帝国的大片领土交给你们。

sentences.en: Now, Salandra expects that to happen.
sentences.zh: 现在，萨兰德拉预料到会这样。

sentences.en: And in fact, he doesn't mind because he's already eyeing up, you know, the Adriatic coaSt.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他并不介意，因为他已经在打亚得里亚海沿岸的主意了，你知道的。

sentences.en: Are the Austrians kind of alerted by this to the possibility that they might jump ship?
sentences.zh: 奥地利人有没有因此而警觉，意识到他们可能会倒戈呢？

sentences.en: Yes, they definitely are.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们绝对警觉了。

sentences.en: They can sort of feel it coming, but they're not going to buy off the Italians by giving them, you know, big chunks of their empire.
sentences.zh: 他们能隐约感觉到风吹草动，但他们绝不会通过割让帝国大片领土来收买意大利人。

sentences.en: I'm just wondering if they're starting to beef up their defenses.
sentences.zh: 我只是想知道他们是否开始加强防御了。

sentences.en: Yeah, they are.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们确实在加强。

sentences.en: But of course, don't forget in this period of time, this is the point that we talked about in our very first First World War series.
sentences.zh: 但当然，别忘了在这段时间里，这就是我们在第一期第一次世界大战系列节目中讨论过的那一点。

sentences.en: But the Russians are coming, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 但俄国人要来了，不是吗？

sentences.en: The Russians are coming.
sentences.zh: 俄国人要来了。

sentences.en: And Tom, you will recall, there's the tremendous battle for the city of Pugimosh.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你一定还记得，那是争夺普吉莫什城的激战。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: How could I forget?
sentences.zh: 我怎么会忘呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Where?
sentences.zh: 哪儿？

sentences.en: Where was it?
sentences.zh: 在哪儿来着？

sentences.en: The fortress city of Pugimosh.
sentences.zh: 要塞城市普吉莫什。

sentences.en: Great to have that back on the show.
sentences.zh: 很高兴这个梗又回到了节目中。

sentences.en: So late February 1915, Salandra's envoys present a secret deal to the allies in London.
sentences.zh: 所以在1915年2月底，萨兰德拉的特使向伦敦的盟友提交了一份秘密协议。

sentences.en: They say, we'll enter the war on the allied side.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们将加入同盟国……不对，是加入协约国一方参战。

sentences.en: And in return, here is our shopping liSt.
sentences.zh: 作为回报，这是我们的购物清单。

sentences.en: We'd like the South Tyrell, we'd like Trentino, we'd like Trieste and Gerizia.
sentences.zh: 我们想要南蒂罗尔，我们想要特伦蒂诺，我们想要的里雅斯特和戈里齐亚。

sentences.en: We'd like Istria, now Croatia.
sentences.zh: 我们想要伊斯特拉，也就是现在的克罗地亚。

sentences.en: We'd like Dalmatia, so that's the coast of Croatia, and the islands.
sentences.zh: 我们想要达尔马提亚，也就是克罗地亚海岸和那些岛屿。

sentences.en: We'd like a little bit of Albania.
sentences.zh: 我们想要阿尔巴尼亚的一小部分。

sentences.en: We'd ideally like the Dodecanese islands of Rhodes, Kos, Patmos, and so on.
sentences.zh: 理想情况下，我们还想要多德卡尼斯群岛的罗德岛、科斯岛、帕特莫斯岛等等。

sentences.en: And we'd like 50 million pounds to pay for the war.
sentences.zh: 我们还想要5千万英镑来支付战争费用。

sentences.en: Now, the Germans have got wind of this.
sentences.zh: 现在，德国人风闻了此事。

sentences.en: They persuade the Austrians to make a generous counteroffer.
sentences.zh: 他们说服奥地利人提出一份丰厚的反报价。

sentences.en: At this point, the Austrians are actually saying to them, okay, we'll give you South Tyrell.
sentences.zh: 此时，奥地利人实际上对他们说，好吧，我们会把南蒂罗尔给你。

sentences.en: We'll give you a bit of Western
sentences.zh: 我们会给你一小部分

sentences.en: Slovenia.
sentences.zh: 斯洛文尼亚。

sentences.en: We will make Trieste autonomous.
sentences.zh: 我们会让的里雅斯特自治。

sentences.en: We can even let you have a little bit of Albania.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至可以让你拥有阿尔巴尼亚的一小部分。

sentences.en: At this point, the Italians are feeling very greedy, and they don't want to accept the Austrian offer.
sentences.zh: 此时，意大利人感到非常贪婪，他们不想接受奥地利的提议。

sentences.en: And they say to the allies, we'd really like to get into bed with you, please.
sentences.zh: 他们对盟友说，我们真的很想和你们上床，求求你们了。

sentences.en: If you give us all this, we'll enter the war.
sentences.zh: 只要你们把这一切都给我们，我们就参战。

sentences.en: And this whole kind of getting into bed with people for money, how does this go down with
sentences.zh: 而这种为了钱跟别人上床的作法，在

sentences.en: people in London and Paris?
sentences.zh: 伦敦和巴黎的人看来是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Well, I'm sorry to say, Tom, that it reinforces existing stereotypes of Italian behavior among the policymakers of London and Paris.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我很遗憾地告诉你，汤姆，这强化了伦敦和巴黎决策者对意大利行为的既有刻板印象。

sentences.en: So when they look at the map, they say, what, you want Dalmatia?
sentences.zh: 所以当他们看地图时，他们会说，什么，你们想要达尔马提亚？

sentences.en: There are 18,000 Italian speakers in Dalmatia, but half a million Slavs.
sentences.zh: 达尔马提亚有18000名意大利语人口，但有50万斯拉夫人。

sentences.en: It seems unreasonable for you to ask for this.
sentences.zh: 你们提出这个要求似乎很不合理。

sentences.en: How can this be justified?
sentences.zh: 这怎么能正当化呢？

sentences.en: Winston Churchill said that Italy was the harlot of Europe.
sentences.zh: 温斯顿·丘吉尔曾说意大利是欧洲的妓女。

sentences.en: So Herbert Henry Asquith, the British Prime
sentences.zh: 所以赫伯特·亨利·阿斯奎斯，英国首相

sentences.en: Minister, of course, a man of the most impeccable moral, sexual behavior.
sentences.zh: 当然，他是一个道德和性行为无可挑剔的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, very much a friend of the show.
sentences.zh: 是的，可以说是本节目的老朋友了。

sentences.en: He described Italy as voracious, slippery, and perfidious.
sentences.zh: 他将意大利描述为贪婪、狡猾和背信弃义。

sentences.en: He wrote the excellent line, it is so important to bring Italy in at once.
sentences.zh: 他写下了这句绝妙的话：立刻把意大利拉拢过来是如此重要。

sentences.en: As greedy and slippery as she is, that we ought not to be too precise in haggling over this or that.
sentences.zh: 尽管她贪婪又狡猾，但我们在讨价还价时实在不宜过于斤斤计较。

sentences.en: Now, of course, this will create great problems in the future when the Italians feel they've been cheated.
sentences.zh: 当然，这将在未来带来巨大的问题，当意大利人觉得自己被欺骗了的时候。

sentences.en: Because at this point, basically, the Allies say, fine, you can have everything you want.
sentences.zh: 因为在这一点上，基本上盟友会说，好吧，你们可以得到你们想要的一切。

sentences.en: Yeah, we'll give you everything.
sentences.zh: 对，我们会把一切都给你。

sentences.en: You can have loads of Croatia, you can have loads of Slovenia.
sentences.zh: 你可以拥有大量的克罗地亚，你可以拥有大量的斯洛文尼亚。

sentences.en: You can actually rule a million Germans and Slavs, if you like, if you really want to that badly.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，如果你真的那么渴望的话，你甚至可以统治一百万德国人和斯拉夫人。

sentences.en: And actually, do you know what?
sentences.zh: 而且事实上，你知道吗？

sentences.en: If the Ottoman Empire falls apart?
sentences.zh: 如果奥斯曼帝国崩溃了？

sentences.en: You can have that as well.
sentences.zh: 你也可以拥有它。

sentences.en: You can have a bit of Turkey as well.
sentences.zh: 你也可以分到一小块土耳其。

sentences.en: Go for it.
sentences.zh: 去吧。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say they don't really mean it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得可以说他们并不是认真的。

sentences.en: They're just promising anything.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在胡乱许诺。

sentences.en: And so, Italy formally repudiates the Triple Alliance.
sentences.zh: 于是，意大利正式宣布废除三国同盟。

sentences.en: So now we're in May.
sentences.zh: 现在我们来到了五月。

sentences.en: And the stage ought to be set for war, but there is a problem.
sentences.zh: 战争本该一触即发，但有一个问题。

sentences.en: First of all, Victor Emmanuel III, with his coins and his very short stature and whatnot, he does not really want the war.
sentences.zh: 首先，维托里奥·埃马努埃莱三世，带着他的硬币、极矮的身材诸如此类的特征，他其实并不想打仗。

sentences.en: He doesn't like the idea of war at all.
sentences.zh: 他一点也不喜欢战争的想法。

sentences.en: More importantly, the Italian people don't really want a war.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，意大利人民其实并不想打仗。

sentences.en: So Solandra asks his regional governors, what do ordinary people think?
sentences.zh: 于是萨兰德拉问他的地方长官，普通民众是怎么想的？

sentences.en: And the governors come back and they say, actually, most people say they don't want to fight.
sentences.zh: 长官们回来报告说，实际上大多数人说他们不想打仗。

sentences.en: They've had a look at the First World War and they think it's possibly not brilliant.
sentences.zh: 他们看过了第一次世界大战，觉得这可能不是个绝妙的主意。

sentences.en: It's probably best to sit this one out.
sentences.zh: 最好还是作壁上观吧。

sentences.en: All that gas and rats and mud and stuff.
sentences.zh: 到处都是毒气、老鼠、泥泞之类的东西。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in the South, in the poorer part of the country, people are really against it.
sentences.zh: 而在南方，也就是国家较贫困的地区，人们强烈反对参战。

sentences.en: So the governor of Naples says 90% of people in the city, including all the social classes, hate the thought of war.
sentences.zh: 因此，那不勒斯的长官说，该市90%的人，包括所有社会阶层，都对战争深恶痛绝。

sentences.en: And basically, across the board, the people who want war are intellectuals, poets,
sentences.zh: 总的来说，支持战争的基本上都是知识分子、诗人，

sentences.en: bad people, Tom.
sentences.zh: 还有些坏蛋，汤姆。

sentences.en: If they're nothing, they don't know.
sentences.zh: 如果他们什么都不是，他们就什么也不知道。

sentences.en: How on earth is the Italian government going to rouse the nation for war?
sentences.zh: 意大利政府究竟要怎样才能唤醒国民去参战呢？

sentences.en: And the answer is by enlisting the most celebrated and colourful and controversial Italian of his generation.
sentences.zh: 答案是，把他们那一代最著名、最具色彩也最具争议的意大利人招致麾下。

sentences.en: And this is this bloke we began with, Gabriele D'Annunzio.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们一开始提到的那个家伙，加布里埃尔·邓邓齐奥（加布里埃尔·邓南遮）。

sentences.en: So D'Annunzio, we did a whole episode on him back in 2022 called The First Fascist with his biographer, Lucy Hughes Hallett.
sentences.zh: 所以邓南遮，我们在2022年曾为他做过一整期节目，邀请他的传记作者露西·休斯-哈利特来聊聊这位“第一位法西斯分子”。

sentences.en: Oh yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: The Pike.
sentences.zh: 《派克》。

sentences.en: Brilliant book.
sentences.zh: 一本精彩的书。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Now, D'Annunzio, for those people who haven't heard that episode, was the most famous
sentences.zh: 现在，对于那些没听过那一期节目的听众来说，邓南遮是当时世界上最著名的

sentences.en: Italian in the world at this point.
sentences.zh: 意大利人。

sentences.en: He's a playwright and a poet.
sentences.zh: 他是一位剧作家和诗人。

sentences.en: He's a dandy.
sentences.zh: 他是个花花公子。

sentences.en: He's a decadent.
sentences.zh: 他是个颓废派。

sentences.en: He's always in the gossip columns.
sentences.zh: 他总是登上八卦专栏。

sentences.en: He's a proper celebrity.
sentences.zh: 他是个名副其实的名人。

sentences.en: I mean, we've been talking about moustaches.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们之前一直在谈论胡须。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He has a brilliant moustache, but it's not a kind of military moustache, is it?
sentences.zh: 他留着一把绝妙的胡子，但这算不上那种军人的胡子，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a kind of the excitement of the new, faintly fascist, flamboyant, let's fly on a plane kind of a moustache.
sentences.zh: 这是一种充满对新事物的兴奋感、隐隐带有法西斯色彩、招摇过市、甚至想开飞机的那种胡子。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: The weird thing about him is, everyone says he's this sort of tremendous, he's always in and out of aristocratic women's bedrooms and stuff.
sentences.zh: 关于他最奇怪的一点是，每个人都说他是个了不起的人物，总是在贵族妇女的卧室里进进出出。

sentences.en: He's a very short man.
sentences.zh: 他个子非常矮。

sentences.en: He's got no hair at all.
sentences.zh: 他几乎没有头发。

sentences.en: He's extremely ugly.
sentences.zh: 他极其丑陋。

sentences.en: People always comment on how terrible his teeth are.
sentences.zh: 人们总是评论他的牙齿有多糟糕。

sentences.en: And he's so narcissistic and egotistical that he's practically sociopathic.
sentences.zh: 而且他极度自恋和自负，简直到了反社会的程度。

sentences.en: It gives us all hope.
sentences.zh: 这让我们所有人都看到了希望。

sentences.en: His life is strewn with wreckage.
sentences.zh: 他的人生布满了残骸。

sentences.en: So basically bad debts, broken homes, abandoned children.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是巨额债务、破碎的家庭、被遗弃的孩子。

sentences.en: He's just a terrible, terrible person.
sentences.zh: 他简直是个无可救药的混蛋。

sentences.en: But because he writes, I mean, the stuff when you actually read it, it's dated really badly.
sentences.zh: 但因为他会写作，我是说，当你真正去读他的东西时，会发现它们过时得厉害。

sentences.en: It's so lush and ornate and stuff.
sentences.zh: 词藻过于华丽繁复。

sentences.en: But he's very highly rated, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 但他评价很高，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, Joyce thinks he's great.
sentences.zh: 我是说，乔伊斯觉得他很伟大。

sentences.en: Proust thinks he's great.
sentences.zh: 普鲁斯特觉得他很伟大。

sentences.en: I mean, they love him.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们都很崇拜他。

sentences.en: People think he's a genius.
sentences.zh: 人们认为他是天才。

sentences.en: People think he's one of the authentic literary geniuses of the early 20th century.
sentences.zh: 人们认为他是20世纪初真正的文学天才之一。

sentences.en: He's gone off to Paris to escape his creditors, but people adore him and women in particular can't get enough of him.
sentences.zh: 他为了躲避债主跑去了巴黎，但人们依然崇拜他，尤其是女性对他爱不释手。

sentences.en: Now, D'Annunzio is an ultra-nationaliSt.
sentences.zh: 现在，邓南遮是一个极端民族主义者。

sentences.en: D'Annunzio has been writing about glory, national and personal, since he was a little boy.
sentences.zh: 邓南遮从小就在写关于国家和个人荣耀的文章。

sentences.en: Ever since the 1880s, he's been pouring out newspaper articles, wittering on about the army and the navy and the air force, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 自1880年代以来，他一直在滔滔不绝地发表报纸文章，喋喋不休地谈论陆军、海军和空军，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because he's very, very keen on planes.
sentences.zh: 因为他非常非常热衷于飞机。

sentences.en: He never learns to fly, but he's obsessed by air power.
sentences.zh: 他从没学会开飞机，但他对空中力量着迷不已。

sentences.en: He is.
sentences.zh: 的确如此。

sentences.en: He's very much of that kind of futurist mentality where everything is about new technology and the excitement of war and all of this.
sentences.zh: 他非常符合那种未来主义的心态，一切都关于新技术、战争的刺激感诸如此类。

sentences.en: Although he is quite keen on kind of ancient dreams of empire as well, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 尽管他对那种古老的帝国梦想也相当热衷，不是吗？

sentences.en: He is.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's the sort of fusion of the two.
sentences.zh: 这是两者的某种融合。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that's how he's the proto-fasciSt.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是他被称为原型法西斯分子的原因。

sentences.en: Quite fascistic.
sentences.zh: 相当具有法西斯色彩。

sentences.en: He was very keen on conquering Libya in 1911.
sentences.zh: 他在1911年就非常热衷于征服利比亚。

sentences.en: He's been talking for ages.
sentences.zh: 他已经唠叨了好久了。

sentences.en: Let's have an empire in the Balkans.
sentences.zh: 让我们在巴尔干建立一个帝国吧。

sentences.en: He was very keen on joining the First World War.
sentences.zh: 他非常热衷于加入第一次世界大战。

sentences.en: And he actually said, I won't come home until we join the war.
sentences.zh: 他甚至说过，在我们参战之前我绝不回家。

sentences.en: But I fear that the Italian political class are too weak.
sentences.zh: 但我担心意大利的政客太软弱了。

sentences.en: And we never will.
sentences.zh: 我们永远也加入不了。

sentences.en: And then in March 1915, he opens a letter in Paris that has been lying around for weeks and is laying kind of unopened.
sentences.zh: 然后，在1915年3月，他在巴黎拆开了一封搁置了几个星期、一直未拆封的信件。

sentences.en: And it's an invitation to come and speak at an event in May just outside Genoa.
sentences.zh: 那是一份邀请函，邀请他在五月去热那亚郊外的一个活动上演讲。

sentences.en: This is the place from which Garibaldi and his volunteers had sailed to Sicily in 1860.
sentences.zh: 这就是1860年加里波第和他的志愿者们扬帆起航前往西西里岛的地方。

sentences.en: And they're going to inaugurate a monument and they want Donancio to come and give a talk.
sentences.zh: 他们要去为一座纪念碑揭幕，并希望多农齐奥来发表讲话。

sentences.en: And he thinks, well, this is it.
sentences.zh: 他心想，机会来了。

sentences.en: This is a brilliant opportunity to come and preach my warlike message to the Italian people.
sentences.zh: 这是向意大利人民宣扬我好战思想的绝佳机会。

sentences.en: So he gets on a train in Paris on the 3rd of May, 1915.
sentences.zh: 于是，他在1915年5月3rd登上了一列开往巴黎的火车。

sentences.en: He crosses the Italian border for the first time in five years.
sentences.zh: 这是他五年来首次穿过意大利边境。

sentences.en: He is met by colossal crowds.
sentences.zh: 迎接他的是黑压压的人群。

sentences.en: He's a sort of, Lucy Hughes
sentences.zh: 他有点像露西·休斯

sentences.en: Hallett in a book calls him a nationalist messiah.
sentences.zh: 哈利特在书中称他为民族主义的弥赛亚。

sentences.en: It's like the prophet returning to his people.
sentences.zh: 这就像先知回归他的子民。

sentences.en: Massive crowds of sort of poets and intellectuals cheering excitedly.
sentences.zh: 成群结队的诗人和知识分子兴奋地欢呼着。

sentences.en: Your vibe.
sentences.zh: 很有你的风格。

sentences.en: It's like when we arrive to do a Restless History tour, surely.
sentences.zh: 这肯定就像我们去进行“不安的历史”巡演时一样。

sentences.en: He gets to Genoa, massive crowds, and he gives the firSt. There'll be a lot of blood-curdling speeches.
sentences.zh: 他抵达热那亚，人山人海，并发表了第...会有很多耸人听闻的演讲。

sentences.en: He gives the first of a series of mad speeches.
sentences.zh: 他发表了一系列疯狂演讲中的第一场。

sentences.en: We shall not let Italy be dishonoured.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不让意大利蒙羞。

sentences.en: We shall not let the fatherland perish.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不让祖国灭亡。

sentences.en: We shall have a greater Italy, not by acquisition, but by conquest, not measured in shame, but as the price of blood and glory.
sentences.zh: 我们将拥有一个更伟大的意大利，不是通过收购，而是通过征服，其代价不是耻辱，而是血与荣耀。

sentences.en: I mean, nobody ever talks more enthusiastically about blood and glory than this bloke.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从来没有人比这家伙更热烈地谈论鲜血和荣耀了。

sentences.en: Next day, he goes to the monument to do the unveiling to give the speech.
sentences.zh: 第二天，他去纪念碑主持揭幕并发表讲话。

sentences.en: And the speech was meant to be all about Garibaldi.
sentences.zh: 这场演讲本该全关于加里波第。

sentences.en: And actually, it's just all about war and how brilliant war is.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，通篇都在谈论战争以及战争有多么精彩。

sentences.en: He ends with this peroration that even though I've, you know, read it many times and written about it in
sentences.zh: 他以这样的经文结束，尽管我，你知道的，读过很多次，并且在

sentences.en: my kid's book about the First World War, I still actually find shocking every time I look at it, because it's a parody of the Sermon on the Mount in favour of fighting and killing.
sentences.zh: 我写给孩子的关于第一次世界大战的书里写过，但每次看我依然觉得震惊，因为这是对《登山宝训》的恶搞，却是为了支持战斗和杀戮。

sentences.en: Blessed are the 20-year-olds, pure of mind, well-tempered in body with courageous mothers.
sentences.zh: 福哉20岁青年，心智纯洁，体魄强健，母亲勇敢。

sentences.en: Blessed are the young who hunger and thirst for glory, for they should be satisfied.
sentences.zh: 福哉渴望荣耀的年轻人，因为他们终将心满意足。

sentences.en: Blessed are the merciful, for they shall wipe away a splendid flow of blood and bind up their shining wounds.
sentences.zh: 福哉仁慈之人，因为他们将拭去奔涌的鲜血并包扎闪光的伤口。

sentences.en: Blessed are they who return with victories, for they shall see the new face of Rome.
sentences.zh: 福哉凯旋而归之人，因为他们将看到罗马的新面貌。

sentences.en: And people complain, don't they?
sentences.zh: 人们会抱怨，不是吗？

sentences.en: And he kind of basically says, you know, if it's wrong to incite people to violence, then so be it.
sentences.zh: 而他基本上就是说，你知道的，如果煽动人们暴力是错的，那就错吧。

sentences.en: I plead guilty.
sentences.zh: 我认罪。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 精彩。

sentences.en: Let's have more of it.
sentences.zh: 让我们多来点这个。

sentences.en: Exactly, he does.
sentences.zh: 没错，他确实这么做了。

sentences.en: And one of the men in his audience that day is a young journalist with a very dark future.
sentences.zh: 那天台下的一名观众是一个有着黑暗未来的年轻记者。

sentences.en: And this is a young man, 33 years old, called Benito Mussolini.
sentences.zh: 这是一个33岁的年轻人，名叫贝尼托·墨索里尼。

sentences.en: And Mussolini had been an editor of the socialist newspaper Avanti.
sentences.zh: 墨索里尼曾是社会主义报纸《前进报》的编辑。

sentences.en: He is absolutely typical of this intellectual class.
sentences.zh: 他完全是这种知识分子阶层的典型代表。

sentences.en: He's read Marx and Engels.
sentences.zh: 他读过马克思和恩格斯。

sentences.en: Mussolini, he's a big fan of Italian futurist poetry.
sentences.zh: 墨索里尼，他是意大利未来主义诗歌的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: Like D'Annunzio, he's obsessed with Nietzsche, the sort of Darwinian idea of struggle and...
sentences.zh: 和达能齐奥一样，他痴迷于尼采，痴迷于那种达尔文主义的斗争思想，以及……

sentences.en: Will to power.
sentences.zh: 权力意志。

sentences.en: The will to power.
sentences.zh: 权力意志。

sentences.en: Hates George Eliot.
sentences.zh: 讨厌乔治·艾略特。

sentences.en: Does Mussolini hate George Eliot?
sentences.zh: 墨索里尼讨厌乔治·艾略特吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, despises her.
sentences.zh: 对，鄙视她。

sentences.en: Wow, why?
sentences.zh: 哇，为什么？

sentences.en: Doesn't like Middlemarch?
sentences.zh: 不喜欢《米德尔马契》？

sentences.en: He thinks that she's very ostentatiously given up Christianity, but she's still completely
sentences.zh: 他认为她非常炫耀地放弃了基督教，但她骨子里依然完全是个

sentences.en: Christian.
sentences.zh: 基督徒。

sentences.en: And she's an idiot because she hasn't realised that's a problem.
sentences.zh: 而她是个笨蛋，因为她没有意识到这是个问题。

sentences.en: He's always going on about it.
sentences.zh: 他总是喋喋不休地谈论这个。

sentences.en: Crikey.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Well, Mussolini had always been a non-interventioniSt. He'd been opposed to Italy's adventures in Africa.
sentences.zh: 好吧，墨索里尼一直是个非干预主义者。他一直反对意大利在非洲的冒险行动。

sentences.en: He said he didn't want to join the First World War.
sentences.zh: 他说他不想加入第一次世界大战。

sentences.en: But then in October
sentences.zh: 但随后在10月

sentences.en: 1914, he sort of sensed the way the wind was blowing and he decided to completely change his mind.
sentences.zh: 1914年，他似乎嗅出了风向，并决定彻底改变主意。

sentences.en: I mean, I guess that's the mark of a good journalist, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想这就是一个好记者的标志，对吧？

sentences.en: I suppose, yes.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: I suppose that's one way of looking at it.
sentences.zh: 我想这是看待问题的一种方式。

sentences.en: But I didn't think we'd be into rehabilitating Mussolini.
sentences.zh: 但我没想到我们会去为墨索里尼翻案。

sentences.en: Well, I'm not.
sentences.zh: 哦，我没有。

sentences.en: His journalistic acumen.
sentences.zh: 我是说他的新闻敏锐度。

sentences.en: I mean, newspapers have been known to kind of jump on bandwagons before.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，报纸以前也是有过随波逐流的前科的。

sentences.en: They have indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So he founds a new newspaper and he sets up his own political movement,
sentences.zh: 所以他创办了一份新报纸，并建立了自己的政治运动，

sentences.en: Mussolini arguing for war, with some French and British allied funding, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，墨索里尼主张战争，并得到了部分英法盟友的资金资助。

sentences.en: And he calls it the Leagues of Revolutionary Action, the Fascidazione Revoluzionaria.
sentences.zh: 他将其命名为革命行动同盟，即Fascidazione Revoluzionaria。

sentences.en: Fascid, meaning the kind of bands or leagues.
sentences.zh: Fascid，意思是类似同盟或联盟的组织。

sentences.en: And it's from that, of course, that we get the word fascism.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们所说的“法西斯主义”这个词就是由此而来的。

sentences.en: Anyway, at this point, Mussolini is just in the crowd.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，此时的墨索里尼还只是人群中的一员。

sentences.en: The star is Danunzio.
sentences.zh: 主角是达农齐奥。

sentences.en: Danunzio gives these impassioned speeches to vast crowds.
sentences.zh: 达农齐奥向庞大的人群发表了这些充满激情的演讲。

sentences.en: He gets a train to Rome.
sentences.zh: 他坐火车去罗马。

sentences.en: He arrives in Rome.
sentences.zh: 他抵达罗马。

sentences.en: 100,000 people awaiting.
sentences.zh: 10万人翘首以盼。

sentences.en: Massive crush.
sentences.zh: 人山人海。

sentences.en: Massive crowds.
sentences.zh: 黑压压的人群。

sentences.en: Gives these speeches again.
sentences.zh: 再次发表这些演讲。

sentences.en: Now, he's starting to denounce what he sees as the traitors, the odour of treachery that is beginning to stifle us.
sentences.zh: 现在，他开始谴责他所看到的叛徒，那开始令人窒息的背叛气味。

sentences.en: And by the traitors, he means the politicians who might actually block the attempt to get into war.
sentences.zh: 他所指的叛徒，是指那些可能会阻挠参战企图的政客们。

sentences.en: Because right now, politics in Rome is very delicately poised.
sentences.zh: 因为眼下，罗马的政坛形势极其微妙。

sentences.en: Because the same day he arrives, the 12th of May, the Italian parliament opens for a new session.
sentences.zh: 因为就在他到达的同一天，即5月12日，意大利议会召开了新一届会议。

sentences.en: And the stakes are very high.
sentences.zh: 而且赌注非常高。

sentences.en: Salandra has done this deal with the allies, but he doesn't have a majority.
sentences.zh: 萨兰德拉与盟友达成了这项协议，但他没有多数席位。

sentences.en: And Rome is awash with rumours that he will fall from power.
sentences.zh: 罗马到处都在流传他将下台的传言。

sentences.en: And he will be replaced by the liberal leader, who is a man called Giovanni Giulitti.
sentences.zh: 他将被自由派领袖吉奥瓦尼·久利蒂取代。

sentences.en: Giulitti has been prime minister four times already, and he does not want to enter the war.
sentences.zh: 久利蒂已经四次担任首相，他不想参战。

sentences.en: So he's not a Danunzio fan.
sentences.zh: 所以他不是达农齐奥的粉丝。

sentences.en: He's not a Danunzio fan.
sentences.zh: 他不是达农齐奥的粉丝。

sentences.en: I think it would have been a lot better if Giulitti had become prime minister and actually hadn't entered the war.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果久利蒂当上首相并且真的没有参战，情况会好得多。

sentences.en: Anyway, the next day, the 13th, Salandra pulls off a great political coup, a great bit of political theatre.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，第二天，即13日，萨兰德拉上演了一场伟大的政治政变，一场伟大的政治戏剧。

sentences.en: He unexpectedly resigns, along with his whole cabinet.
sentences.zh: 他出人意料地同整个内阁一起辞职。

sentences.en: And he's basically daring the king to appoint Giulitti as prime minister and Giulitti to accept the job.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是在挑衅国王任命久利蒂为首相，并让久利蒂接受这份工作。

sentences.en: And he's betting that they will be put off by the mood on the streets.
sentences.zh: 他笃定他们会被街头的狂热气氛吓退。

sentences.en: These huge crowds are pouring through the streets of Rome, shouting, death to Giulitti, up with the war, all this thing.
sentences.zh: 这些庞大的人群涌入罗马街头，高喊着打倒久利蒂、支持战争等等。

sentences.en: And Danunzio is going around the city, giving these bonkers speeches.
sentences.zh: 达农齐奥则在城里四处游走，发表这些荒唐的演讲。

sentences.en: The treachery is blatant.
sentences.zh: 背叛昭然若揭。

sentences.en: We don't only breathe in its horrid stench.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅能闻到它那可怕的恶臭。

sentences.en: We feel its appalling weight.
sentences.zh: 我们更能感受到它那骇人的分量。

sentences.en: I tell you, there is treason here in Rome.
sentences.zh: 我告诉你们，罗马这里有叛徒。

sentences.en: We're being sold like a herd of diseased cattle.
sentences.zh: 我们正像一群病牛一样被出卖。

sentences.en: And Danunzio, again a prefiguring of fascism, he says to the crowds, form squads, lie in wait, seize them, by which he means Giulitti and the anti-war politicians,
sentences.zh: 达农齐奥再次预示了法西斯主义，他对人群说，组建小队，设伏，抓住他们，他指的是久利蒂和反战政客们，

sentences.en: capture them, and all this.
sentences.zh: 抓获他们，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Didn't Mussolini call him the John the Baptist of fascism?
sentences.zh: 墨索里尼不是称他为法西斯的施洗者约翰吗？

sentences.en: Yes, he did.
sentences.zh: 是的，他确实这么叫过。

sentences.en: Well, he absolutely is the John the Baptist of fascism.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他绝对就是法西斯的施洗者约翰。

sentences.en: If Danunzio had been left to his own devices, he would have been the John the Baptist and the Jesus of fascism.
sentences.zh: 如果听凭达农齐奥自行其是，他本可以成为法西斯的施洗者约翰和耶稣。

sentences.en: But he is outsmarted by Mussolini.
sentences.zh: 但他被墨索里尼智胜了。

sentences.en: He goes on to set up his kind of mad regime in Fiume, doesn't he, after the war?
sentences.zh: 战后他继续在阜姆建立他那种疯狂的政权，不是吗？

sentences.en: He does, which is a massive prefiguring of Mussolini, actually, where he calls himself the
sentences.zh: 他确实这么做了，这实际上极大程度地预示了墨索里尼，他在那里自称为

sentences.zh: 领袖。

sentences.en: So anyway, he's giving these crazy speeches.
sentences.zh: 总之，他在发表这些疯狂的演讲。

sentences.en: Blood will flow, but blood will be blessed, all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 鲜血将流淌，但鲜血将受到祝福，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And the crowd's getting more and more impassioned.
sentences.zh: 人群变得越来越狂热。

sentences.en: Giulitti, the anti-war politician, goes to see the king, and he says, I can't take office against this backdrop.
sentences.zh: 反战政客久利蒂去见国王，他说，在这种背景下我无法上台执政。

sentences.en: You know, there'll be a nationalist rebellion.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，会发生民族主义叛乱。

sentences.en: There could be civil war.
sentences.zh: 可能会爆发内战。

sentences.en: I don't want to do it.
sentences.zh: 我不想这么做。

sentences.en: And so on the 16th, the king reinstates Salandra as prime minister.
sentences.zh: 于是，在16日，国王恢复了萨兰德拉的首相职务。

sentences.en: And the king says to Parliament, I think you're just going to have to vote for the war.
sentences.zh: 国王对议会说，我想你们只能投票赞成战争。

sentences.en: And I'll abdicate if you don't, because the king has lost his nerve himself.
sentences.zh: 如果你们不投，我就退位，因为国王自己已经失去了勇气。

sentences.en: As another nationalist journalist puts it in his newspaper, either Parliament will prostitute the sacred, trembling body of the nation to the foreigner.
sentences.zh: 正如另一位民族主义记者在报纸上所说，要么议会将出卖国家神圣颤抖的躯体给外国人。

sentences.en: I mean, that rhetoric is so kind of 1910s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这种修辞太具有1910年代的风格了。

sentences.en: Or the nation will overthrow Parliament, overturning the benches of the moneylenders, purifying the dens of the pimps and pandas with iron and fire.
sentences.zh: 要么国家将推翻议会，掀翻放债人的长椅，用铁与火净化皮条客和拉皮条者的巢穴。

sentences.en: I mean, it is amazing the kind of the twisting of language from the New Testament to promote war.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，把新约圣经的话语扭曲来宣扬战争，这真是太令人惊叹了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I know.
sentences.zh: 是的，我知道。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: It's extraordinary, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这太不寻常了，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, of all these deranged speeches, probably, I mean, I think this is one of the worSt. This is Denunzio.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在所有这些精神错乱的演讲中，大概，我认为这是最糟糕的一个。这是达农齐奥。

sentences.en: He goes to the Capitoline Hill, where, as you said, they've been building that giant sort of wedding cake, this sort of symbol of Italian nationalism.
sentences.zh: 他去了卡比托利欧山，正如你所说，他们一直在那里建造那个巨大的像结婚蛋糕一样的建筑，这是意大利民族主义的一种象征。

sentences.en: And he whips his crowd, this giant crowd into a frenzy.
sentences.zh: 他煽动着他的民众，这庞大的人群陷入狂热。

sentences.en: He says, the old order must be totally destroyed.
sentences.zh: 他说，旧秩序必须彻底摧毁。

sentences.en: We must cast aside the politicians like rotten meat.
sentences.zh: 我们必须像扔掉烂肉一样抛弃政客。

sentences.en: Sweep away all the filth into the sewer with all that is vile.
sentences.zh: 把所有的污秽和下流东西一起扫进下水道。

sentences.zh: 他说，意大利将在烈火中重生。

sentences.en: He says again and again, he calls it the HolocauSt.
sentences.zh: 他一次又一次地称之为大屠杀。

sentences.zh: 这是达农齐奥最喜欢的词之一。

sentences.en: He says, let's drive out the anti-war politicians.
sentences.zh: 他说，让我们赶走反战政客。

sentences.en: Yeah, they're not just wrong.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们不仅是错的。

sentences.en: They are sick.
sentences.zh: 他们是有病的。

sentences.en: They are diseased.
sentences.zh: 他们是腐化的。

sentences.en: We should drive them out of politics forever.
sentences.zh: 我们应该将他们永远驱逐出政坛。

sentences.en: Make lists.
sentences.zh: 列出黑名单。

sentences.en: Proscribe them.
sentences.zh: 公开流放他们。

sentences.en: Be pitiless.
sentences.zh: 毫不留情。

sentences.en: Like Sulla or the second triumvirate.
sentences.zh: 就像苏拉或前三头同盟那样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Then at the end, I mean, this is also, it feels very Roman.
sentences.zh: 然后最后，我的意思是，这也是，感觉非常罗马。

sentences.en: He takes out a sword that had belonged to an Ogaribald, his lieutenants.
sentences.zh: 他拿出一把曾属于加里波第的副手的宝剑。

sentences.en: And he says, Italy will be born again in blood.
