sentences.zh: 然而，卡多纳却对他的政治上司说，如果一切顺利，我们将在——引述原话——

sentences.en: The heart of the Habsburg monarchy, which is to say Vienna, by the autumn.
sentences.zh: 在秋天之前抵达哈布斯堡王朝的心脏，也就是维也纳。

sentences.en: We'll be there.
sentences.zh: 我们会到那里的。

sentences.en: We will genuinely be there and done and dusted by Christmas.
sentences.zh: 到圣诞节时，我们肯定已经打到那里并大获全胜了。

sentences.en: I mean, an absolutely ridiculous thing for him to say.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他说出这种话简直荒谬至极。

sentences.en: The campaign starts badly, as you might expect, and it gets worse.
sentences.zh: 正如你所料，这场战役开局不利，而且情况越来越糟。

sentences.en: Because the Italian railways aren't really up to it.
sentences.zh: 因为意大利的铁路系统根本不堪重负。

sentences.en: The full mobilization that was meant to take three weeks goes on for more than six weeks.
sentences.zh: 原本计划三周完成的全面动员，持续了六个多星期。

sentences.en: We said that the Austrians are distracted by fighting Russia in the eaSt.
sentences.zh: 我们说过，奥地利人因为要在东线与俄国作战而分身乏术。

sentences.en: So this was Italy's moment.
sentences.zh: 所以这是意大利的绝佳时机。

sentences.en: Italy actually outnumbered the Austrians four to one on their kind of common frontier.
sentences.zh: 在他们所谓的共同边界上，意大利的兵力实际上达到了奥地利人的四倍。

sentences.en: But because they're so slow and disorganized, they don't exploit their advantage at all.
sentences.zh: 但由于他们行动迟缓、毫无组织，完全没有利用好这一优势。

sentences.en: I mean, let's cheer the Austrians up, who've been completely useless so far in the war, haven't they?
sentences.zh: 我是说，让我们为奥地利人鼓个劲吧，他们在战争至今的表现简直一无是处，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: To find that they've got an enemy who are even worse than them.
sentences.zh: 结果发现他们遇到了一个比自己还要糟糕的敌人。

sentences.en: We're going to see the Austrians in a very different light in today's episode.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我们将会以全新的视角看待奥地利人。

sentences.en: The Austrians will appear to be the souls of sort of military competence.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人将展现出某种军事素养的精髓。

sentences.en: Martial competence.
sentences.zh: 军事能力。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，一点没错。

sentences.en: So Cadorna's initial target, he says, well, the first thing we'll do is we will cross the river Socha or Isonzo.
sentences.zh: 因此，卡多纳最初的目标是，他说，好吧，我们要做第一件事就是渡过索查河或伊松佐河。

sentences.en: So Socha in Slovenian, Isonzo in Italian, which goes through the valleys of western Slovenia, quite close to the border.
sentences.zh: 也就是斯洛文尼亚语中的索查河，意大利语中的伊松佐河，它流经斯洛文尼亚西部山谷，离边境很近。

sentences.en: I was actually there last summer, this part of the world.
sentences.zh: 去年夏天我其实去过那里，世界上的这个地方。

sentences.en: It's very beautiful, isn't it, Slovenia?
sentences.zh: 非常美，对吧，斯洛文尼亚？

sentences.en: Incredibly beautiful.
sentences.zh: 美得难以置信。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, a brilliant place.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一个绝佳的地方。

sentences.en: I should be doing an advert for the Slovenian Tourist Board.
sentences.zh: 我应该去为斯洛文尼亚旅游局拍个广告。

sentences.en: Well, if the Slovenian Tourist Board are listening, I would love to go.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果斯洛文尼亚旅游局在听的话，我很乐意去。

sentences.en: I've always wanted to go.
sentences.zh: 我一直都想去。

sentences.en: I keep kind of mapping out, you know, fortnights when I could go and I never do.
sentences.zh: 我总是盘算着，你知道的，计划哪两周可以去，但总是没去成。

sentences.en: It's gorgeous.
sentences.zh: 那里美极了。

sentences.en: And it's, they've turned the whole thing basically into a First World War sort of tourist attraction.
sentences.zh: 而且他们基本上把整个地方都变成了一个类似于第一次世界大战的旅游景点。

sentences.en: So there are military cemeteries.
sentences.zh: 所以那里有军人公墓。

sentences.en: There's amazing like trench networks and forts.
sentences.zh: 还有惊人的战壕网和堡垒之类的东西。

sentences.en: You can roam around to your heart's content.
sentences.zh: 你可以尽情地四处闲逛。

sentences.en: In the most, it's a lot better than the Western Front because it's much more beautiful.
sentences.zh: 最棒的是，它比西线好得多，因为风景要美得多。

sentences.en: It's brilliant, actually.
sentences.zh: 真的很棒。

sentences.en: I really recommend it.
sentences.zh: 我极力推荐。

sentences.en: And everything is really lovely.
sentences.zh: 而且一切都非常可爱。

sentences.en: Nice weather, nice people.
sentences.zh: 天气很好，人也很好。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: But a very different scene back in 1915, right?
sentences.zh: 但在1915年的那个时候，情景却截然不同，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly, yes.
sentences.zh: 没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: Not if you're Italian in 1915.
sentences.zh: 如果你在1915年是个意大利人，那就另当别论了。

sentences.en: So basically, the Italians were meant to cross this river straight away.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，意大利人本该立刻渡过这条河。

sentences.en: The Austrians blew up the bridges.
sentences.zh: 但奥地利人炸毁了桥梁。

sentences.en: It took the Italians ages to get across.
sentences.zh: 意大利人花了很长时间才过去。

sentences.en: By the time they get across, the Austrians are dug in on the mountains above.
sentences.zh: 等他们渡过河时，奥地利人已经在上方的群山中掘壕据守了。

sentences.en: And this will be the focus of the campaign for the next two years.
sentences.zh: 这将成为未来两年战役的焦点。

sentences.en: So the valley of this river, the Socho or the Isonzo, and above it, the jagged kind of limestone highlands.
sentences.zh: 也就是这条河——索查河或伊松佐河的山谷，以及它上方那片崎岖的石灰岩高地。

sentences.en: So what is called the Karst or the Karso.
sentences.zh: 也就是所谓的喀斯特地貌。

sentences.en: I mean, that's what you want to see when you are launching a full frontal attack.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是你发动正面进攻时最想看到的。

sentences.en: A jagged limestone highland.
sentences.zh: 一片崎岖的石灰岩高地。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Oh, God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Last episode, we did the Western Front and you probably thought that sounded bad with all the mud and the lice and stuff.
sentences.zh: 上集我们讲了西线，你可能觉得那里到处是泥泞和虱子，听起来糟透了。

sentences.en: But at least it's flat.
sentences.zh: 但至少那里地势平坦。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is much worse.
sentences.zh: 对，这里要糟糕得多。

sentences.en: Much worse.
sentences.zh: 糟糕得多。

sentences.en: So basically, in the summer, it is ridiculously hot.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，夏天热得离谱。

sentences.en: It's like the sun blazing down as you stagger up these kind of limestone hills.
sentences.zh: 当你踉踉跄跄地爬上这些石灰岩山丘时，烈日当空照。

sentences.en: In the winter, it's ridiculously cold, the wind whipping in off the Adriatic or whatever.
sentences.zh: 冬天冷得要命，从亚得里亚海刮来的狂风肆虐呼啸。

sentences.en: Because it's limestone, you can't really dig proper trenches.
sentences.zh: 因为是石灰岩地质，你根本无法挖掘像样的战壕。

sentences.en: So you can dig a sort of little gully and lie down in this gully.
sentences.zh: 所以你只能挖一个小沟渠，然后躺在这个沟里。

sentences.en: And when bullets and shells hit the ground, they send up showers of fragments.
sentences.zh: 当子弹和炮弹击中地面时，会激起阵阵碎片。

sentences.en: Yeah, limestone shards in your eye.
sentences.zh: 没错，石灰岩碎片会飞进你的眼睛里。

sentences.en: That's not what you want.
sentences.zh: 这可不是你想要的。

sentences.en: Well, these shards would kill people half a mile away.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些碎片能在半英里外致人死命。

sentences.en: Oh, God.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: Yeah, if you're standing with your back to what's going on half a mile away, this shard will hit you in the back of the head and that's the end of you.
sentences.zh: 对，如果你背对着半英里外发生的交火站着，这块碎片就会击中你的后脑勺，然后你就完蛋了。

sentences.en: Do you remember in the previous series, I asked why the people didn't try and outflank the bottom of the Western Front by invading Switzerland?
sentences.zh: 你还记得在前一季里，我问过为什么人们不尝试通过入侵瑞士来迂回西线的底部吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 记得。

sentences.en: And I guess that this is the explanation, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我想这就是原因吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Don't go through mountains.
sentences.zh: 千万别穿过山脉。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So for the first few weeks, the Italians go extremely slowly.
sentences.zh: 所以在最初的几周里，意大利人的推进速度极其缓慢。

sentences.en: They capture only a few villages and a few small towns.
sentences.zh: 他们只占领了几个村庄和小镇。

sentences.en: They lose 20,000 men in the first few weeks.
sentences.zh: 他们在头几周就损失了两万名士兵。

sentences.en: They show absolutely no sign of having any conception of how they're going to take on machine guns and barbed wire and all this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们完全没有表现出任何概念，不知道该如何应对机枪、铁丝网以及诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: And Cadorna, General Cadorna with his nice mustache and whatnot, he looks at this and he says, well, I'm obviously not going to rethink my tactics because my tactics are excellent.
sentences.zh: 而卡多纳，蓄着漂亮胡子之类的卡多纳将军，看到这一幕后说，好吧，我显然不会重新考虑我的战术，因为我的战术棒极了。

sentences.en: What I should do is just start sacking generals.
sentences.zh: 我应该做的就是开始撤换将军。

sentences.en: So in two years, he launches what Mark Thompson calls a rolling purge of his officers.
sentences.zh: 因此在两年时间里，他展开了马克·汤普森所称的对军官的滚动清洗。

sentences.en: In two years, he sacks 217 generals, 255 colonels and 355 battalion commanders.
sentences.zh: 在两年里，他撤换了217名将军、255名上校和355名营长。

sentences.en: Seems a lot to me, especially with already disorganized army.
sentences.zh: 在我看来这数量惊人，特别是对一个本来就缺乏组织的军队而言。

sentences.en: I mean, 217 generals, that's a lot of generals.
sentences.zh: 我是说，217名将军，那可是相当多的将军了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I feel that Italians probably have too many generals.
sentences.zh: 我觉得意大利人大概有太多的将军了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's like the Royal Navy now with about 700 admirals and three ships.
sentences.zh: 对，这就像现在的英国皇家海军，拥有大约700名海军将领和3艘军舰。

sentences.en: It's kind of on brand, though, for the Italians to have loads of generals, though, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 不过，意大利人拥有大量将军倒也很符合他们的风格，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's a lot of gold braid, a lot of nice hats and feathers and stuff, I imagine.
sentences.zh: 我想象那里有许多金色的穗带、漂亮的帽子和羽毛之类的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Now, while the Italians are sacking their generals and basically trudging very slowly up these hills, the Austrians have been moving reinforcements to the front.
sentences.zh: 好了，正当意大利人撤换将军并且极其缓慢地在这些山丘上艰难跋涉时，奥地利人一直在向前方调集增援部队。

sentences.en: Now, as we said, people will recall, the Austrians have had an absolutely shocking start to the war.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，大家会记起，奥地利人在战争刚开始时的表现简直令人震惊。

sentences.en: They made an absolute spectacle of themselves against Serbia.
sentences.zh: 他们在对阵塞尔维亚时简直成了一场笑柄。

sentences.en: And basically ends up losing to Serbia, which is insane, given that that was the point of the whole war.
sentences.zh: 结果基本上输给了塞尔维亚，考虑到那是整场战争的起因，这简直太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Then they had a nightmare against Russia on the Eastern Front.
sentences.zh: 接着他们在东线对阵俄国时遭遇了一场噩梦。

sentences.en: You will recall a very, very fine mustache belonging to France Conrad von Hutzendorf, the Austrian supreme commander.
sentences.zh: 你们会记得弗朗茨·康拉德·冯·赫岑多夫——奥地利最高指挥官，留着非常非常漂亮的胡子。
zh_words: 弗朗茨·康拉德·冯·赫岑多夫

sentences.en: Is he the guy who is besotted with, what's her name, Gina?
sentences.zh: 他是那个迷恋上一个叫什么名字的女人——吉娜的家伙吗？

sentences.en: Gina.
sentences.zh: 吉娜。

sentences.en: That's why he started the war.
sentences.zh: 这就是他挑起战争的原因。

sentences.en: And he basically starts the First World War, just to impress her.
sentences.zh: 他挑起第一次世界大战，基本上就是为了给留下深刻印象。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He started the First World War, just to impress Gina von Reininghaus, who is, ironically, Italian.
sentences.zh: 他挑起第一次世界大战，仅仅是为了给吉娜·冯·雷宁豪斯留下好印象，而讽刺的是，她是个意大利人。

sentences.en: Oh, I didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 哦，我不知道这件事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Remember, Conrad von Hutzendorf had wanted to invade everybody, had demanded about 6,000 times to attack Austria's neighbours before the war finally started.
sentences.zh: 记住，在战争最终爆发前，康拉德·冯·赫岑多夫曾想入侵所有人，并曾大约6000次要求攻击奥地利的邻国。

sentences.en: By 1915, he's lost his youngest son on the Eastern Front, and he's managed to mislay 800,000 men who've been killed, basically the entire pre-war Austro-Hungarian army.
sentences.zh: 到了1915年，他在东线失去了小儿子，并且成功弄丢了80万阵亡士兵，基本上相当于战前整个奥匈帝国的军队。

sentences.en: But this is the one thing that he gets right, the Italian campaign.
sentences.zh: 但这是他做对的一件事，即意大利战役。

sentences.en: Is Gina impressed?
sentences.zh: 吉娜印象深刻吗？

sentences.en: Must be very impressed.
sentences.zh: 肯定印象非常深刻。

sentences.en: Even though he's fighting the Italians, her own people?
sentences.zh: 尽管他打的是意大利人，也就是她自己的同胞？

sentences.en: I think by this point she's gone native a bit.
sentences.zh: 我想到了这个时候，她已经有点融入当地了。

sentences.en: But it's still tragic that the one thing he gets right is against Gina's countrymen.
sentences.zh: 但唯一做对的一件事竟然是针对吉娜的同胞，这仍然是个悲剧。

sentences.en: Yeah, maybe, maybe.
sentences.zh: 是的，也许吧，也许是这样。

sentences.en: It's a tragedy there.
sentences.zh: 这确实是个悲剧。

sentences.en: So what he does is, Conrad von Hutzendorf, he's finally learned the lessons, and he says, we're not going to attack, we're just going to be on the defensive, what we have we hold.
sentences.zh: 所以他所做的是，康拉德·冯·赫岑多夫终于吸取了教训，他说，我们不再进攻了，我们只进行防御，守住我们已有的阵地。

sentences.en: And he sends to defend the River Isonzo, the most senior South Slav officer in the Imperial Army.
sentences.zh: 他派去防守伊松佐河的，是帝国军队中资历最深的南斯拉夫族军官。

sentences.en: And Dominic, whom is he, and how do you pronounce his name?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，他是谁？他的名字该怎么发音？

sentences.en: He is a name to conjure with, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，他可是一个大名鼎鼎的人物。

sentences.en: He's General Svetozar Borovic.
sentences.zh: 他就是斯韦托扎尔·博罗维奇将军。

sentences.en: So General Borovic is one of the outstanding generals of the First World War.
sentences.zh: 所以博罗维奇将军是第一次世界大战中最杰出的将军之一。

sentences.en: And he is the kind of embodiment of Austro-Hungarian multi-ethnic unity, because he was born in Croatia to a Serbian Orthodox family.
sentences.zh: 他可以说是奥匈帝国多民族团结的化身，因为他出生于克罗地亚的一个塞尔维亚东正教家庭。

sentences.en: He joined the army when he was 10, went to cadet school.
sentences.zh: 他10岁就加入了军队，进入了士官学校。

sentences.en: He was first decorated in the capture of Sarajevo in 1878 in Bosnia.
sentences.zh: 他在1878年波斯尼亚萨拉热窝的攻占行动中首次获得勋章。

sentences.en: And because he's a South Slav, yeah, because he's basically the embodiment of what would become Yugoslavia, he's really invested in this campaign,
sentences.zh: 由于他是南斯拉夫族人，对，因为他基本上就是日后将成为南斯拉夫的化身，他对这场战役投入了极大的热情，

sentences.en: because he's defending Slavic territory.
sentences.zh: 因为他在保卫斯拉夫人的领土。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to see the Italians.
sentences.zh: 他不想看到意大利人。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He kind of sees all this.
sentences.zh: 他某种程度上看清了这一切。

sentences.en: And most of his men, or at least a lot of his men, are Slovenes, Croats, and Bosnians.
sentences.zh: 而且他的大部分士兵，或者至少很大一部分士兵，都是斯洛文尼亚人、克罗地亚人和波斯尼亚人。

sentences.en: So they're also fighting for land that feels like theirs.
sentences.zh: 所以他们也是在为他们觉得属于自己的土地而战。

sentences.en: So they're really invested in this.
sentences.zh: 因此他们对这场战役非常投入。

sentences.en: General Paul von Hindenburg, German walrus, he said of the Austro-Hungarians, they fought the Russians with their head, but fought the Italians with their whole soul.
sentences.zh: 德国海象——保罗·冯·兴登堡将军曾这样评价奥匈帝国人：他们用头脑与俄国人作战，却用整个灵魂与意大利人作战。

sentences.en: And I guess that's because they're not actually really Austro-Hungarians, as you said.
sentences.zh: 我想那是因为正如你所说，他们其实并不是真正的奥匈帝国人。

sentences.en: They are Slavs defending a Slav homeland.
sentences.zh: 他们是保卫斯拉夫家园的斯拉夫人。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: But also, Borowievich is a smart guy.
sentences.zh: 但同时，博罗维奇是个聪明人。

sentences.en: Like, he's one of the generals who's learned the lessons of the war.
sentences.zh: 你看，他是吸取了战争教训的将军之一。

sentences.en: He says, okay, what we'll do is, we'll get as high as we can.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，我们要做的就是，尽量占据高处。

sentences.en: We'll have five lines of barbed wire.
sentences.zh: 我们要设置五道铁丝网防线。

sentences.en: Let the Italians come.
sentences.zh: 让意大利人来吧。

sentences.en: When they come, wait until they're 100 yards away.
sentences.zh: 等他们发起进攻时，等到他们距离我们100码远时再动弹。

sentences.en: Only start firing then.
sentences.zh: 到那时才开始开火。

sentences.en: If they ever break through, don't panic.
sentences.zh: 如果他们真冲上来了，别慌。

sentences.en: Keep your positions.
sentences.zh: 坚守阵地。

sentences.en: I'll move up the reserves.
sentences.zh: 我把预备队调上去。

sentences.en: I'll plug the gaps.
sentences.zh: 我去填补缺口。

sentences.en: We'll just stay calm.
sentences.zh: 我们保持冷静。

sentences.en: We'll let them come to us, and we'll kill them all.
sentences.zh: 我们引他们过来，然后把他们全歼。

sentences.en: And basically, this is what they do.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，他们就是这么干的。

sentences.en: So the first battle of the Isonzo, as it's called, is launched by the Italians on the 23rd of June, 1915.
sentences.zh: 所以，所谓的第一次伊松佐河战役，是由意大利人于1915年6月23日发起的。

sentences.en: And think of this river.
sentences.zh: 想象一下这条河。

sentences.en: It's running just inside the border of Slovenia, so to the east of Italy.
sentences.zh: 它正好流经斯洛文尼亚边境内部，也就是意大利的东边。

sentences.en: And the Italians throw in more than 200,000 men, which is more than twice as many as the Austrians have got.
sentences.zh: 意大利人投入了二十多万大军，比奥地利人的兵力足足多了一倍还多。

sentences.en: And the Italians think, well, this will go, this will be great.
sentences.zh: 意大利人想，这回行了，这肯定大获全胜。

sentences.en: And actually, what happens, they charge uphill, and the Austrians open fire with their machine guns,
sentences.zh: 然而实际情况却是，他们往山上冲，奥地利人则用机枪开火，

sentences.en: and loads and loads of Italians are killed straight away.
sentences.zh: 成片成片的意大利人瞬间倒在血泊中。

sentences.en: So I'll give you an example, an account by an Italian officer called Renato di Stolfo.
sentences.zh: 我举个例子，看看一个叫雷纳托·迪·斯托尔福的意大利军官的记述。

sentences.en: And he's describing an attack on a mountain called Monte San Michele.
sentences.zh: 他描述的是对一座叫圣米凯莱山的进攻。

sentences.en: Di Stolfo is meant to be leading his men into battle with a pistol.
sentences.zh: 迪·斯托尔福本该手里拿把手枪带领部下冲锋陷阵。

sentences.en: They've run out of pistols, so he only has his sword.
sentences.zh: 但手枪用光了，所以他只有一把军刀。

sentences.en: It starts raining as soon as they set off, so they're all completely sodden and waterlogged.
sentences.zh: 他们刚出发就开始下雨，所以所有人都湿透了，身上沉甸甸的。

sentences.en: They draw their swords, there's a band.
sentences.zh: 他们拔出军刀，还有军乐队。

sentences.en: They're shouting, Savoy, which is their kind of war cry at the house of Savoy.
sentences.zh: 他们高喊着“萨伏依”，这是他们对萨伏依王朝的一种战吼。

sentences.en: They start to go off uphill.
sentences.zh: 他们开始往山上冲。

sentences.en: They're all carrying backpacks that are 35 kilograms in weight.
sentences.zh: 每个人都背着重达35公斤的背包。

sentences.en: What are they taking?
sentences.zh: 他们带的都是些啥？

sentences.en: Pots?
sentences.zh: 锅吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Pasta?
sentences.zh: 意大利面？

sentences.en: Are they eating pasta by this point?
sentences.zh: 他们那时候就吃意大利面吗？

sentences.en: Or isn't that invented by Americans in 1958?
sentences.zh: 难道不是美国人在1958年才发明的吗？

sentences.en: In 1964, yeah.
Yeah, invented in St. Louis, Missouri.
sentences.zh: 对，是在密苏里州圣路易斯发明的。

sentences.en: Isn't that the way with all Italian dishes?
sentences.zh: 所有的意大利菜不都这样吗？

sentences.en: I gather so.
sentences.zh: 我猜是吧。

sentences.en: That's what I vaguely remember.
sentences.zh: 我隐约记得是这样。

sentences.en: No, but 35 kilograms, you know when you check into a plane?
sentences.zh: 不对，35公斤啊，你坐飞机托运行李的时候知道吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I know.
sentences.zh: 知道，我知道。

sentences.en: And the maximum is 23 or something.
sentences.zh: 上限也就23公斤左右。

sentences.en: I wouldn't want to be charging Austrian machine gun placements, you know, with limestone shards going everywhere.
sentences.zh: 我可不想去冲锋奥地利的机枪阵地，周围到处都是飞溅的石灰岩碎块。

sentences.en: You've got the weight of two suitcases, two full suitcases on your back, staggering up this
sentences.zh: 你背上背着两个行李箱的重量，两个满满的行李箱，踉踉跄跄地爬上这...

sentences.en: lime, you know, it's raining, soon the sun's going to come out and then you'll be steaming or whatever.
sentences.zh: 石灰岩，你知道的，正在下雨，一会儿太阳一出来你身上就得冒热气什么的。

sentences.en: What the hell are they taking?
sentences.zh: 他们到底带了些什么鬼东西？

sentences.en: Anyway, they stagger up this hill.
sentences.zh: 总之，他们跌跌撞撞地爬上这座山。

sentences.en: Then the Austrians start shooting at them.
sentences.zh: 接着奥地利人开始向他们开枪。

sentences.en: Most of the officers were killed straight away.
sentences.zh: 大部分军官当场阵亡。

sentences.en: The men are all scrambling around on their hands and knees to take cover.
sentences.zh: 士兵们手脚并用到处寻找掩护。

sentences.en: And Di Stolfo said, in a whirl of death and glory, within a few moments, the epic Garibaldian style of warfare is crushed and consigned to the shadows of history.
sentences.zh: 迪·斯托尔福说，在死亡与荣耀的旋风中，短短几分钟内，加里波第式的史诗战争风格就被粉碎，并被送入了历史的阴影之中。

sentences.en: And basically, there's then another rainstorm which stops the battle and the Italian survivors
sentences.zh: 基本上，接着又下了一场雨，战斗被迫暂停，活下来的意大利士兵

sentences.en: sort of stagger back down the hill with their backpacks and they're back to where they started.
sentences.zh: 背着背包踉踉跄跄地退下山，又回到了出发的地方。

sentences.en: And this is the story of the entire first battle of the Isonzo.
sentences.zh: 这就是整个第一次伊松佐河战役的故事。

sentences.en: It takes two weeks.
sentences.zh: 持续了两周。

sentences.en: The Italians make about two yards and they take 15,000 casualties.
sentences.zh: 意大利人只推进了大约两码，却付出了15000人的伤亡。

sentences.en: That's the first battle of the Isonzo.
sentences.zh: 这就是第一次伊松佐河战役。

sentences.en: And how many are there going to be over the course of the war?
sentences.zh: 在接下来的战争进程中还会有多少次？

sentences.en: There's going to be 11 more of them.
sentences.zh: 还将会有11次。

sentences.en: You would think if you were General Cadorna, you would say, well, that didn't work.
sentences.zh: 你要是卡多尔纳将军，你肯定会想，这行不通啊。

sentences.en: I probably won't try that again.
sentences.zh: 我大概不会再试一次了。

sentences.en: He tries it 11 more times in the next two years or so.
sentences.zh: 他在接下来的两年左右里又试了11次。

sentences.en: Well, he's written his book.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他的书已经写好了。

sentences.en: He has written his book.
sentences.zh: 他的书确实写好了。

sentences.en: But also, while this was happening, he was at a conference with the Allied generals, the British and the French.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，在发生这一切的同时，他正在与盟军将军（英国和法国人）开会。

sentences.en: And they said to him, we want you to, you know, now you've entered the war, we've given you this money and these promises.
sentences.zh: 他们对他说，我们希望你，既然你已经参战了，我们给了你资金和承诺。

sentences.en: You need to, you know, produce results.
sentences.zh: 你需要，你知道的，拿出成果来。

sentences.en: So he feels under pressure.
sentences.zh: 所以他感到压力很大。

sentences.en: And so less than two weeks later, he launches the second battle of the Isonzo, again in the Socha Valley.
sentences.zh: 因此不到两周后，他又发动了第二次伊松佐河战役，地点同样在索查河谷。

sentences.en: Same story.
sentences.zh: 历史总是惊人地相似。

sentences.en: Up the hill they go, cut down by Austrian machine guns.
sentences.zh: 他们冲上山，被奥地利人的机枪肆意屠杀。

sentences.en: And they haven't advanced at all.
sentences.zh: 而且他们根本没有取得任何进展。

sentences.en: I mean, barely.
sentences.zh: 我是说，几乎没有。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, if you get really into the weeds of this, you'll find they've actually captured...
sentences.zh: 我是说，你要是深入研究这些细节，就会发现他们其实攻占了……

sentences.en: A village or something.
sentences.zh: 一个村庄什么的。

sentences.en: A village, a hill here, a hill there.
sentences.zh: 一个村庄，这里一个山头，那里一个山头。

sentences.en: But in the grand scheme of things, they've made no progress whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 但在宏大的战略格局下，他们根本没有取得任何实质进展。

sentences.en: The sun has come out.
sentences.zh: 太阳出来了。

sentences.en: These amazing accounts from officers in Mark Thompson's book.
sentences.zh: 马克·汤普森的书里记录了这些来自军官的惊人见证。

sentences.en: There's no escaping the heat.
sentences.zh: 酷热难耐，无处可藏。

sentences.en: Tongues swell, coated with thick saliva.
sentences.zh: 舌头肿胀，覆盖着厚厚的唾液。

sentences.en: Fingers swell and dangle clumsily from sticky hands.
sentences.zh: 手指肿胀，无力地垂在黏糊糊的手掌上。

sentences.en: Eyes inflamed, skin like parchment.
sentences.zh: 眼睛发炎，皮肤像羊皮纸一样。

sentences.en: And he also quotes an Italian officer called Virgilio Bonamore, who kept a diary in the first month of the war.
sentences.zh: 他还引用了一位名叫维吉利奥·博纳莫雷的意大利军官的话，他在战争头一个月里写了日记。

sentences.en: Bonamore says, you know, he describes being in one of these limestone trenches.
sentences.zh: 博纳莫雷说，他描述了自己身处这些石灰岩战壕之一的情景。

sentences.en: We talked about the trenches on the Western Front last time.
sentences.zh: 我们上次讨论过西线战场的战壕。

sentences.en: The Italian trenches are awful.
sentences.zh: 意大利人的战壕糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: They are far worse than anything on the Western Front.
sentences.zh: 比西线战场的任何战壕都要糟糕得多。

sentences.en: Because they can't dig down deep enough, really, for them to be effective.
sentences.zh: 因为他们根本无法向下挖得足够深，以发挥实际效用。

sentences.en: They can't dig down.
sentences.zh: 他们根本挖不深。

sentences.en: You can't bury the bodies.
sentences.zh: 你也没法埋葬尸体。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.en: So the bodies are just hanging around.
sentences.zh: 所以尸体就那样到处都是。

sentences.en: The stench was unbearable, says Bonamore.
sentences.zh: 恶臭令人窒息，博纳莫雷说。

sentences.en: We're squatting among our own and enemy corpses.
sentences.zh: 我们蹲在自己人和敌人的尸体堆里。

sentences.en: Basically, you can't get very deep.
sentences.zh: 基本上，战壕挖不深。

sentences.en: So when the Austrians fire at you, lots of you end up dying.
sentences.zh: 所以当奥地利人向你开火时，你们很多人最终都会丧命。

sentences.en: Blokes are being ripped open by shells and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 小伙子们被炮弹和其他武器撕裂。

sentences.en: And he gives us a description of a single day on the Opussocha River on the 14th of AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 他向我们描述了8月14日在奥普索查河畔的一整天。

sentences.en: Gives you a sense of what it's like.
sentences.zh: 让你体会一下那是什么样的情景。

sentences.en: So the Italians started with an artillery bombardment at three o'clock in the morning.
sentences.zh: 意大利人于清晨三点开始进行炮击。

sentences.en: And they set off uphill.
sentences.zh: 然后他们开始向山上挺进。

sentences.en: Before they even really started uphill, most of them were absolutely exhausted.
sentences.zh: 甚至在他们真正开始上山之前，大部分人就已经精疲力竭了。

sentences.en: And some of them, while they're walking, fell asleep while they were walking, which seems a bit much.
sentences.zh: 其中一些人在行军时竟然一边走一边睡着了，这简直有点不可思议。

sentences.en: The sun finally comes up.
sentences.zh: 太阳终于升起来了。

sentences.en: And they discover that they're on this hillside.
sentences.zh: 他们发现自己处在这个山坡上。

sentences.en: They're totally exposed.
sentences.zh: 他们完全暴露了。

sentences.en: There's no cover.
sentences.zh: 没有任何掩体。

sentences.en: They're exposed to the Austrian guns.
sentences.zh: 他们完全暴露在奥地利人的枪口下。

sentences.en: The Austrians fire at them and kind of rake them with shrapnel.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人向他们开火，用榴霰弹对他们进行疯狂扫射。

sentences.en: But that goes on till midday.
sentences.zh: 这种情况一直持续到中午。

sentences.en: And then at midday, their officer says,
sentences.zh: 然后到了中午，他们的军官说，

sentences.en: OK, charge now.
sentences.zh: 好了，现在冲锋。

sentences.en: They start charging.
sentences.zh: 他们开始冲锋。

sentences.en: The people who've got the wire cutters are all shot down before they even get to the barbed wire.
sentences.zh: 带着剪线钳的人还没到达铁丝网就被全部击毙了。

sentences.en: So the rest of the men then are underneath the barbed wire.
sentences.zh: 于是剩下的士兵只好躲在铁丝网下面。

sentences.en: And the Austrian machine guns are just firing at them.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人的机枪疯狂地向他们扫射。

sentences.en: Bonamore.
sentences.zh: 博纳莫雷写道。

sentences.en: The dead are in piles on top of each other.
sentences.zh: 尸体层层叠叠堆成小山。

sentences.en: Nearly all the senior officers have fallen.
sentences.zh: 高级军官几乎全部阵亡。

sentences.en: And basically, they end up huddling for hours together, kind of underneath the Austrian barbed wire.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们最后只能挤在一起好几个小时，躲在奥地利人的铁丝网下。

sentences.en: They can't get through it.
sentences.zh: 他们冲不过去。

sentences.en: They can't go back.
sentences.zh: 也退不回来。

sentences.en: They're kind of stuck.
sentences.zh: 他们就这样被困住了。

sentences.en: They all run out of ammo.
sentences.zh: 他们的弹药全部耗尽。

sentences.en: And their captain says, I think we should just make a break for it.
sentences.zh: 他们的连长说，我觉得我们应该找机会突围。

sentences.en: We should try to sneak away.
sentences.zh: 我们应该试着悄悄溜走。

sentences.en: And so they start to sneak away.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始悄悄撤离。

sentences.en: The first four men who try to sneak away are all shot straight away.
sentences.zh: 头四个试图溜走的士兵当场就被全部击毙了。

sentences.en: Actually, let's not sneak away.
sentences.zh: 好吧，还是别溜了。

sentences.en: This is a really bad idea.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是个馊主意。

sentences.en: So they basically just stay there under the Austrian wire until darkness comes.
sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上只能一直待在奥地利人的铁丝网下，直到天黑。

sentences.en: And then when darkness comes, and the Austrians have kind of gone to bed or whatever, they manage to stumble down the hill.
sentences.zh: 天黑之后，奥地利人大概去睡觉了什么的，他们才设法踉踉跄跄地摸下山。

sentences.en: And Bonamore says in his diary, what a massacre.
sentences.zh: 博纳莫雷在日记里写道，这是一场多么残酷的大屠杀。

sentences.en: How many young lives wasted?
sentences.zh: 多少年轻的生命白白消逝？

sentences.en: It's raining nonstop.
sentences.zh: 雨下个不停。

sentences.en: And we lie in the bottom of a ravine to spend the night amid the water and the cold.
sentences.zh: 我们躺在峡谷底部，在冰冷刺骨的水中度过了一个夜晚。

sentences.en: And the amazing detail about all this, about these battles that always sticks in my mind.
sentences.zh: 关于这一切，关于这些战斗，最让我记忆犹新、感到惊奇的一个细节是。

sentences.en: It's very unusual in the story of the First World War.
sentences.zh: 这在第一次世界大战的历史中非常罕见。

sentences.en: There are loads of stories about the Austrians saying to the Italians, go back.
sentences.zh: 有很多关于奥地利人对意大利人喊话的故事，叫他们回去。

sentences.en: We won't shoot at you.
sentences.zh: 我们不会向你们开枪。

sentences.en: You know, don't kill yourselves for nothing.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，别白白送死了。

sentences.en: So here's an example.
sentences.zh: 这里有个例子。

sentences.en: An Austrian captain shouting to his machine gunners.
sentences.zh: 一个奥地利连长朝他的机枪手大喊。

sentences.en: He says to them, what do you want to do?
sentences.zh: 他对他们说，你们想怎么样？

sentences.en: Do you want to kill them all?
sentences.zh: 你们想把他们全杀光吗？

sentences.en: Let them be.
sentences.zh: 放过他们吧。

sentences.en: And then he says to the Italians, stop, go back.
sentences.zh: 然后他对意大利人喊道，停下，回去吧。

sentences.en: We won't shoot anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们不再开枪了。

sentences.en: Do you want everyone to die?
sentences.zh: 你们想让所有人都死在这里吗？

sentences.en: Loads of accounts of the Austrians saying, Italians, go back.
sentences.zh: 有大量记录显示奥地利人在喊：意大利人，回去吧。

sentences.en: We don't want to massacre you.
sentences.zh: 我们不想屠杀你们。

sentences.en: Your brave men don't get yourselves killed like this.
sentences.zh: 你们这些勇敢的小伙子，别这么白白送命了。

sentences.en: And there's even a story from later in the year.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有一年晚些时候的故事。

sentences.en: The Austrians actually stopped firing during a battle.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人竟然在战斗中主动停火了。

sentences.en: And they said to the Italians, go on.
sentences.zh: 他们对意大利人说，上吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, enough.
sentences.zh: 行了，够了。

sentences.en: Get your dead and go back down.
sentences.zh: 抬上你们的死者，退回去。

sentences.en: And as the Italians were collecting all their dead, the Austrians came out from behind their machine guns to help them, to bring them stretchers and cigarettes.
sentences.zh: 正当意大利人收敛阵亡士兵的尸体时，奥地利人从机枪后面走出来帮助他们，给他们送去担架和香烟。

sentences.en: And the Italians gave them some of their feathers from their plumed hats as nice souvenirs.
sentences.zh: 而意大利人则把羽毛帽上的一些羽毛送给对方作为美好的纪念品。

sentences.en: God, they're still wearing plumed hats after all this.
sentences.zh: 天呐，经历这一切后他们竟然还在戴羽毛帽。

sentences.en: They're still wearing their plumed hats.
sentences.zh: 他们居然还在戴着羽毛帽。

sentences.en: I mean, what are they thinking?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们到底在想什么？

sentences.en: So that was the second battle.
sentences.zh: 所以那是第二次战役。

sentences.en: The second battle was a massive bloodbath.
sentences.zh: 第二次战役是一场巨大的血腥屠杀。

sentences.en: The Italians lost 42,000 men.
sentences.zh: 意大利人损失了四万两千人。

sentences.en: The Austrians actually lost more, 50,000.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人的损失其实更大，达到了五万人。

sentences.en: So here is the question.
sentences.zh: 所以问题来了。

sentences.en: It's been agitating Callum, our producer.
sentences.zh: 这让我们的制作人卡勒姆一直很纠结。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: How come the Austrians actually lost more?
sentences.zh: 为什么奥地利人的损失反而更大？

sentences.en: Because they're outnumbered.
sentences.zh: 因为他们寡不敌众。

sentences.en: And because the Italians, when they finally do get their act together, they're able to overrun some Austrian positions.
sentences.zh: 而且因为意大利人在终于振作起来的时候，能够攻占一些奥地利人的阵地。

sentences.en: But they aren't able to do enough of that to swing the tide of the battle.
sentences.zh: 但他们做不到足够多来扭转战局。

sentences.en: But, I mean, let's not pretend that the Austrians aren't going...
sentences.zh: 不过，我是说，我们别假装奥地利人没有……

sentences.en: The Austrians are being killed too, in large numbers.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人也在被大量杀害。

sentences.en: You know, the Austrians, they're not exactly one of Europe's great military machines.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，奥地利人可谈不上是欧洲什么伟大的军事机器。

sentences.en: We saw how badly they performed against the Russians.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了他们在对阵俄国人时的表现有多糟糕。

sentences.en: They are struggling, but somehow they're clinging on, is the answer.
sentences.zh: 他们在苦苦挣扎，但不知怎么还是死死支撑着，这就是答案。

sentences.en: So they are the massive underdogs here, even though they're at the top of the hill.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在这里是绝对的弱势方，尽管他们占据着山头。

sentences.en: But this slightly recalibrates the strategy then.
sentences.zh: 但这稍微重新调整了战略。

sentences.en: Because it does suggest that, albeit bloodly, it is working.
sentences.zh: 因为这确实表明，尽管付出了血的代价，它正在起作用。

sentences.en: And if the Austrians are as outnumbered as they seem to be...
sentences.zh: 如果奥地利人真的像看上去那样寡不敌众的话……

sentences.en: One day it will work.
sentences.zh: 总有一天会奏效的。

sentences.en: One day it would work.
sentences.zh: 总有一天会起作用的。

sentences.en: I mean, you can kind of see...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你多少能看出……

sentences.en: Cadorna's mentality.
sentences.zh: 卡多尔纳的心态。

sentences.en: General Cadorna's spin doctor joins us now on the rest of his history.
sentences.zh: 卡多尔纳将军的形象公关现在加入了我们的“余下的历史”。

sentences.en: Yeah, but it doesn't work, though.
sentences.zh: 对，但它其实没起作用。

sentences.en: I mean, I would say it doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为它没用。

sentences.en: Well, we'll see.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们拭目以待。

sentences.en: We'll see.
sentences.zh: 我们走着瞧。

sentences.en: I think the fact that the Italians, despite all this, are losing fewer men than the Austrians does put a slightly different perspective on it.
sentences.zh: 我认为尽管如此，意大利人损失的人数比奥地利人少，这一点确实让事情有了点不同的视角。

sentences.en: But they're not always losing fewer men.
sentences.zh: 但他们并不总是损失更少的人。

sentences.en: So back in Rome, Salandra, the prime minister, is becoming very frustrated.
sentences.zh: 所以回到罗马，首相萨兰德拉变得非常沮丧。

sentences.en: He needs a victory to show the Italian public, but he also needs a victory to appease the Allies.
sentences.zh: 他需要一场胜利来向意大利公众交代，他也需要一场胜利来安抚盟友。

sentences.en: So, in October, General Cadorna agrees to launch a third battle of the Isonzo.
sentences.zh: 因此，在十月份，卡多尔纳将军同意发起第三次伊松佐河战役。

sentences.en: And it starts with a huge bombardment in October the 18th.
sentences.zh: 它始于十月十八日的一场大规模轰炸。

sentences.en: Not enough, as always, to break the Austrian defences or destroy their barbed wire.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样，根本不足以打破奥地利人的防御或摧毁他们的铁丝网。

sentences.en: The Italians advance through driving rain.
sentences.zh: 意大利人在强降雨中推进。

sentences.en: Two weeks.
sentences.zh: 两周过去了。

sentences.en: It's really muddy.
sentences.zh: 到处都是泥泞。

sentences.en: They don't really get anywhere.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没推进到哪去。

sentences.en: And that's that.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样。

sentences.en: And at the end of that third battle, the Italians lost maybe 67,000 men killed and wounded.
sentences.zh: 在那场第三次战役结束时，意大利人伤亡人数可能达到了六万七千人。

sentences.en: But in this case, only 40,000 Austrians.
sentences.zh: 但这一次，只有四万名奥地利人伤亡。

sentences.en: So, the tide of war is turning.
sentences.zh: 所以，战争的局势正在转变。

sentences.en: Well, now, you would think at this point Cadorna would surely change tactics.
sentences.zh: 好了，现在你本会认为到了这个时候卡多尔纳肯定会改变战术。

sentences.en: But no, he looks at the calendar.
sentences.zh: 但并没有，他看了看日历。

sentences.en: He says, well, it's probably time for a fourth battle before the end of the year.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，大概是时候在年底前发动第四次战役了。

sentences.en: And he's convinced the Austrians must be running out of men now.
sentences.zh: 他确信奥地利人现在一定人手不足了。

sentences.en: And he's not entirely wrong, because in some places, the Italians outnumber the Austrians three to one.
sentences.zh: 他也不完全是错的，因为在某些地方，意大利人的兵力是奥地利人的三倍。

sentences.en: So, he launches a fourth battle.
sentences.zh: 于是，他发起了第四次战役。

sentences.en: At this point, it's now very cold.
sentences.zh: 此时，天气已经非常寒冷。

sentences.en: Lots of the Italians have got frostbite.
sentences.zh: 许多意大利士兵都冻伤了。

sentences.en: Their feet are so swollen with frostbite, they can't put their boots on.
sentences.zh: 他们的脚被冻疮肿得连靴子都穿不上。

sentences.en: Their hands are all purple and misshapen with the cold.
sentences.zh: 他们的双手被冻得发紫且严重变形。

sentences.en: Lots of Italians by now have started to shoot themselves to get out of the war.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，许多意大利人已经开始对自己开枪以逃避这场战争。

sentences.en: So, given the choice, you would rather be fighting at the Battle of Luce than in this battle?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果有得选，你宁愿去打卢斯战役而不是这场战役？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是的。

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Because, here's the teSt.
sentences.zh: 因为，考验来了。

sentences.en: First, when Allied observers went to the Italian lines, they said, oh my God, I didn't think anything could be worse than what we're experiencing.
sentences.zh: 首先，当盟军观察员去到意大利军队的防线时，他们说，哦天哪，我以为没有什么会比我们经历过的更糟了。

sentences.en: But this is absolutely awful.
sentences.zh: 但这里简直糟透了。

sentences.en: So, in that fourth battle, by the way, the Italians lost 49,000 men, the Austrians 30,000.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，在那第四次战役中，意大利人损失了四万九千人，奥地利人损失了三万.

sentences.en: So, again, the Italians lost more.
sentences.zh: 所以，意大利人再次伤亡更多。

sentences.en: And the conditions in the Italian trenches over the winter were absolutely appalling.
sentences.zh: 而且冬天意大利战壕里的条件简直糟得骇人。

sentences.en: They have these shallow trenches.
sentences.zh: 他们的战壕挖得很浅。

sentences.en: Their uniforms are in rags.
sentences.zh: 他们的制服破烂不堪。

sentences.en: A lot of them don't even have guns.
sentences.zh: 他们中的许多人甚至没有枪。

sentences.en: Their boots fall apart.
sentences.zh: 他们的靴子都散架了。

sentences.en: They've all got typhoid and cholera.
sentences.zh: 他们都染上了伤寒和霍乱。

sentences.en: And actually, the thing that, I was about to say, amuses me, it both appalls and amuses me.
sentences.zh: 事实上，让我，我正想说，这既让我感到震惊又觉得好笑。

sentences.en: British visitors who went to the Italian cab so they couldn't get over the toilet conditions.
sentences.zh: 去过意大利营地的英国参观者简直无法接受那里的厕所条件。

sentences.en: That they had no respect for Italian hygiene.
sentences.zh: 他们对意大利的卫生状况毫无敬意。

sentences.en: One British visitor said, the Italian camp was literally a field of filth.
sentences.zh: 一位英国参观者说，意大利营地简直就是一片污秽的场地。

sentences.en: I had never seen such a disgusting sight.
sentences.zh: 我从未见过如此令人作呕的景象。

sentences.en: And I wondered what kind of epidemic was being bred amidst the excreta and soiled paper.
sentences.zh: 我在想，在排泄物和沾满污物的纸张中到底滋生了什么样的瘟疫。

sentences.en: I mean, it sounds like a kind of Baideker discussing Italian toilet arrangements.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这听起来就像某种贝德克尔旅游指南在讨论意大利的厕所安排。

sentences.en: It so does.
sentences.zh: 太像了。

sentences.en: 1897 or something.
sentences.zh: 1897年左右什么的。

sentences.en: They're always very sniffy about that.
sentences.zh: 他们对那种事总是非常挑剔。

sentences.en: Or a columnist in the Daily Telegraph whose children have just been to Glastonbury and is appalled by that.
sentences.zh: 或者就像《每日电讯报》的一位专栏作家，他的孩子刚去过格拉斯顿伯里音乐节并对此感到震惊。

sentences.en: When he went to see if they were getting on.
sentences.zh: 当他去查看他们过得怎么样时。

sentences.en: Anyway, so the year ends with the war in total deadlock at an absolutely horrendous coSt.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，这一年就在战争陷入彻底僵局和绝对惨重的代价中结束了。

sentences.en: So the Italians have now lost, killed and wounded 400,000 men.
sentences.zh: 因此，意大利人现在已经死伤了四十万人。

sentences.en: And this is a war that they chose, right?
sentences.zh: 而这是一场他们自己选择的战争，对吧？

sentences.en: They could have stayed out, but they've thrown away the lives of all these people.
sentences.zh: 他们本可以置身事外，但他们却白白断送了所有这些人的生命。

sentences.en: And Mark Thompson gives the example of a single brigade who were called, unimprovably, the Polenta Brigade because they wore yellow colours.
sentences.zh: 马克·汤普森举了一个营的例子，他们被极其贴切地称为“玉米粥营”，因为他们穿着黄色的军服。

sentences.en: And the Polenta Brigade began the war with 130 officers and 6,000 soldiers.
sentences.zh: “玉米粥营”参战时拥有130名军官和6000名士兵。

sentences.en: And by the end of 1915, having been reinforced several times, they have lost 154 officers and 4,276 men killed, wounded and missing.
sentences.zh: 到1915年底，在经过多次兵力补充后，他们已经阵亡、受伤和失踪了154名军官和4276名士兵。

sentences.en: So almost the entire, you know, the entire pre-war contingent.
sentences.zh: 所以几乎把所有的，你知道的，战前的整个编制都拼光了。

sentences.en: And so by the end of the year, the Italians have actually lost more than the Austrians, do you think?
sentences.zh: 所以在年底的时候，你觉得意大利人的损失实际上比奥地利人还要多吗？

sentences.en: Yes, they have.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And just to look ahead, in the next two years, they fight another eight battles on the Isonzo.
sentences.zh: 展望未来，在接下来的两年里，他们在伊松佐河又打了另外八场战役。

sentences.en: And basically the 12th of them, the Italians just crack completely and the Austrians end up winning it.
sentences.zh: 基本上到了第十二场，意大利人的防线彻底崩溃，奥地利人最终赢得了胜利。

sentences.en: And this is at a place called Cobberid, very pretty town actually.
sentences.zh: 这是在一个叫科博里德的地方，实际上是个非常美丽的小镇。

sentences.en: Caporetto, Hemingway was there towards the end of the war.
sentences.zh: 卡波雷托，海明威在战争快结束时曾在那里。

sentences.en: This is what he's, when he writes about the Italian front, he's writing about Caporetto.
sentences.zh: 这就是他，当他写到意大利前线时，他写的就是卡波雷托。

sentences.en: And the Italian Second Army was completely destroyed.
sentences.zh: 意大利第二集团军被彻底消灭了。

sentences.en: And the Austrians and the Germans, who have now piled in to help the Austrians, they pushed them back and they struck 100 miles into Italy.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人和现在赶来支援奥地利人的德国人将他们击退，并深入意大利境内100英里。

sentences.en: And then the Austrians themselves then fell apart.
sentences.zh: 然后奥地利人自己也崩溃了。

sentences.en: The Italians rallied at the River Piave.
sentences.zh: 意大利人在皮亚韦河重新集结。

sentences.en: And then they beat the Austrians at Vittorio Veneto in November of 1918.
sentences.zh: 然后在1918年11月的维托里奥威内托战役中击败了奥地利人。

sentences.en: And this was the point at which the Austro-Hungarian Empire was falling apart.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，奥匈帝国正在瓦解。

sentences.en: And then the war ends.
sentences.zh: 然后战争结束了。

sentences.en: And at that point, the Italians have lost 689,000 people killed in battle, as well as probably about 600,000 civilians and another million Italians seriously wounded.
sentences.zh: 在那时，意大利人在战斗中阵亡了68万9千人，此外还有大约60万平民以及另外一百万重伤的意大利人。

sentences.en: So it goes well.
sentences.zh: 所以进展得真顺利。

sentences.en: Yeah, it didn't exactly develop to their advantage.
sentences.zh: 是的，事情的发展完全没对他们有利。

sentences.en: And it's this tremendous national trauma.
sentences.zh: 这是一次巨大的国家创伤。

sentences.en: And the thing is, for what?
sentences.zh: 关键是，这一切都是为了什么？

sentences.en: Because at the peace conferences, they are given Trieste.
sentences.zh: 因为在和平会议上，他们得到了里雅斯特。

sentences.en: They're given Istria.
sentences.zh: 他们得到了伊斯特拉。

sentences.en: They're given the Trentino and South Tyrell.
sentences.zh: 他们得到了特伦蒂诺和南蒂罗尔。

sentences.en: But they're not given a lot of the other stuff they wanted.
sentences.zh: 但他们并没有得到他们想要的许多其他东西。

sentences.en: They don't get a bit of Turkey.
sentences.zh: 他们没有得到土耳其的一部分。

sentences.en: They don't get loads of Greek islands.
sentences.zh: 他们没有得到大量的希腊岛屿。

sentences.en: They don't get Dalmatia.
sentences.zh: 他们没有得到达尔马提亚。

sentences.en: They don't get an empire in the Adriatic.
sentences.zh: 他们没有在亚得里亚海建立帝国。

sentences.en: And even though on paper they are among the winners of the First World War, lots of Italians feel, we've actually, you know, we did all that for nothing.
sentences.zh: 尽管从纸面上看他们是一战的胜利者之一，但许多意大利人觉得，我们实际上，你知道的，我们白干了这一切。

sentences.en: You know, we didn't get what we wanted.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们没有得到我们想要的。

sentences.en: And so this will feed into feelings of resentment that will help to incubate fascism?
sentences.zh: 所以这会滋生出怨恨情绪，从而有助于孕育法西斯主义吗？

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全如此。

sentences.en: So one of the people who feels cheated is one of the worst men in history,
sentences.zh: 所以觉得受骗的人之一，也是历史上最糟糕的人物之一，

sentences.en: Gabriello D'Annunzio.
sentences.zh: 加布里埃尔·邓邓齐奥。

sentences.en: And he has all the, through the war, he's been reveling in the war.
sentences.zh: 在整场战争中，他一直沉浸在战争的狂热中。

sentences.en: I mean, he was nicknamed the Poet of Slaughter, and he loved that nickname.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他被称为“屠杀诗人”，而且他很喜欢这个绰号。

sentences.en: And when the war ends, because they don't get the Istrian port of Rieca, or Fiume as the Italians called it,
sentences.zh: 当战争结束时，因为他们没有得到伊斯特拉港口里耶卡（意大利人称之为菲乌梅），

sentences.en: he seizes it himself with a parametric group, and he names himself the Duce.
sentences.zh: 他带着一个准军事组织亲自夺取了它，并自封为领袖。

sentences.en: And that, of course, is an inspiration for another man we've mentioned, the man who really does tap the bitterness after Italy's war,
sentences.zh: 当然，这启发了我们提到的另一个人，那个真正利用了意大利战后痛苦的人，

sentences.en: a man who had fought on the Isonzo, who rose to become a corporal, who was badly wounded, but survived to tell the tale.
sentences.zh: 一个曾在伊松佐河作战、晋升为下士、受过重伤但死里逃生的人。

sentences.en: And that man was Benito Mussolini.
sentences.zh: 那个人就是贝尼托·墨索里尼。

sentences.en: Okay, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 好了，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Well, next week we will be leaving the killing fields of the Isonzo and heading out onto the high seas for the story of the Lusitania.
sentences.zh: 好吧，下周我们将离开伊松佐河的杀戮场，前往公海讲述卢西塔尼亚号的故事。

sentences.en: In a way, a sequel, not just to this series, but to the series we did on Titanic, because it involves more death on the high seas.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这不仅是本系列的续集，也是我们制作的泰坦尼克号系列的续集，因为它涉及公海上更多的死亡。

sentences.en: And then after that, we will be going to Brussels for a spy story.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，我们将前往布鲁塞尔讲述一个间谍故事。

sentences.en: Or was Edith Cavell a spy?
sentences.zh: 或者埃迪斯·卡维尔真的是间谍吗？

sentences.en: We will be exploring that.
sentences.zh: 我们将对此进行探讨。

sentences.en: And Restless History Club members, of course, can hear both those episodes and the remaining two episodes, which will be on Gallipoli.
sentences.zh: 当然，“余下的历史”俱乐部成员可以收听这两集以及关于加里波利的其余两集。

sentences.en: So to join them and get the full range of benefits, the only way to do that is to go to therestlesshistory.com and sign up there.
sentences.zh: 所以要加入他们并获得全方位的福利，唯一的途径就是访问therestlesshistory.com并在那里注册。

sentences.en: So thank you, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，多米尼克。

sentences.en: Thank you, everyone, for listening.
sentences.zh: 谢谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: We will be back soon.
sentences.zh: 我们很快就会回来。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Ciao, arrivederci.
sentences.zh: 再见，保重。
